articles.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in Perforce Puppet to execute code on vulnerable servers.
Puppet is an infrastructure-as-code (IaC) and configuration management platform that uses a client-server architecture for device management.
Tracked as CVE-2026-115731 (CVSS score of 9.4), the exploited security defect is described as a deserialization of untrusted data issue in the report processing of Puppet Enterprise and Puppet Core, leading to remote code execution (RCE).
It allows clients that have a certificate signed by the Puppet certificate authority (CA) to send reports containing malicious payloads that would be executed on the server with the service user permissions, putting managed systems at risk.
“A successful attack could expose the server’s certificate-signing key, allow an attacker to issue trusted certificates, and enable changes to software and configuration delivered to managed systems on their next Puppet run,” Perforce explains in an advisory.
Unauthenticated attackers could obtain a certificate if the CA auto-signs requests without performing strong verification. Administrators are advised to turn off auto-signing and enforce strong validation to ensure only trusted systems and authorized users can receive certificates.
The security hole was patched on November 3 alongside CVE-2026-115732, a critical issue where an attacker could use a certificate with a name that extends an approved name to bypass authorization and imperson…

articles.title: Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
articles.summary:
With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass new protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block users from filing lawsuits.
Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more
Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
On Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against users who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. Separately, a few blocks away, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Laurel Lee (R-FL) brought hotel heiress Paris Hilton to Capitol Hill to advocate for the Defiance Act, which would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators.
“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors,” Sen. En face, Aixam, le spécialiste historique, demande 13 999 € pour une e-City Pack. Linktour veut se glisser entre les deux avec l’Alumi, lancée en France le 16 juin 2026 par cette filiale de Shandong Weiqiao Pioneering, un groupe chinois du textile, de l’énergie et de l’aluminium.

articles.title: Tesla peut déployer sa conduite autonome en Finlande, mais la France résiste toujours
articles.summary:
Tesla franchit une nouvelle étape dans le déploiement de son système de conduite autonome en Europe. Le constructeur américain vient d’obtenir le feu vert de Traficom, l’agence finlandaise des transports et des communications. Il pourra prochainement commercialiser son système Tesla Assisted Driving auprès des propriétaires d’environ 6 500 véhicules compatibles. La Finlande rejoint ainsi les dix autres pays européens ayant reconnu l’homologation provisoire délivrée aux Pays-Bas en avril. Mais la France reste encore à convaincre.
Tesla Assisted Driving : ce qui change pour les automobilistes finlandais
Le FSD (Full Self-Driving) de Tesla change de nom et devient Tesla Assisted Driving. Une évolution réclamée par plusieurs responsables politiques européens, qui jugeaient l’ancienne appellation trompeuse pour un système nécessitant toujours la surveillance du conducteur. « Le changement de nom aide les utilisateurs et le marché à comprendre la vraie nature du système », explique Jukka Juhola, expert principal chez Traficom.
La Finlande autorise son déploiement avant même le vote européen. L’agence justifie sa décision par ce changement de nom, mais aussi par les modifications apportées à la gestion de la vitesse. Jusqu’à présent, le FSD pouvait autoriser un dépassement de 50 % de la limitation. Cette marge est désormais réduite à 10 % et revient à zéro à chaque démarrage du véhicule.

For a while there, it seemed like Lenovo had given up on selling handheld gaming PCs, hiking the price of its Legion Go 2 and Legion Go S far higher than other RAM-starved competitors. A decent one can easily cost $1,000 if not $2,000 now. But it looks like Lenovo might be about to announce a relatively cheap handheld once again— the Legion Go Beam.

It looks comparatively cheap — and that might be a good thing in this economy.

While it’s got the same big stippled grips and triggers for comfort, there’s only one USB-C port on the top instead of two, a comparatively cheap-looking D-pad, no touchpad, and only a single tiny intake and exhaust for its fan.
There’s no SteamOS logo where that would go, so it likely runs Windows instead… but then there’s that name, “Beam.” Perhaps you’ll “beam” your games to it because it’s a streaming and cloud gaming handheld, instead of one that primarily plays games on its own chip? articles.title: Sony's updated turntable is an easy entry into the world of vinyl | TechCrunch

Record players and other retro tech are making a strong comeback, and I’ve recently rejoined the world of vinyl collecting. Lately, I’ve noticed myself turning to Spotify less frequently, so it felt like the perfect time to start using a record player again.
Choosing a turntable can be quite overwhelming, especially for beginners. That’s where Sony’s new PS-LX3BT turntable comes in.
Since 2019, Sony’s PS-LX310BT has been a go-to choice for vinyl newbies. Now that it has been discontinued, the PS-LX3BT emerges as its successor, keeping the same beginner-friendly approach while adding a few modern upgrades.
Currently priced at $399.99, the PS-LX3BT is designed for people who want to enjoy vinyl without getting too caught up in the technical side of things. It’s also a good option for those looking to upgrade from their first inexpensive turntable without having to learn how to set up or customize a more complicated audio system.
One of its biggest selling points is how easy it is to use. articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. articles.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Releases Poisoned With Credential Stealer
articles.summary:
Hackers distributed two malicious versions of Microsoft’s Agent Framework Python package through PyPI in a November 17 supply chain attack, potentially exposing cloud and CI/CD credentials belonging to users who installed them.
Microsoft Agent Framework is designed for developing AI agents and multi-agent applications. The affected package, agent-framework, has approximately 190,000 downloads per month.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were released roughly 33 minutes apart. Both have since been quarantined on PyPI, where version 1.26.0 remains the latest clean release.
Microsoft has acknowledged the incident, with an Agent Framework maintainer confirming in a GitHub discussion that the compromised releases were removed from PyPI and that an investigation was underway.
The malicious distributions retained the legitimate framework components while introducing additional code that attempted to steal credentials. This allowed applications to continue functioning normally despite the compromise.
Researchers at OX Security, Wiz, Endor Labs, and SafeDep independently analyzed the malware, which exploits a Python startup mechanism to execute automatically in an affected environment.
The malware runs whenever the Python interpreter starts, even if the application doesn’t explicitly import the compromised package.

articles.title: IKEA, ASOS, Zoom… Plus de 175 sites piratés ont peut-être tenté de voler vos données bancaires
articles.summary:
Comme le révèle l’entreprise de cybersécurité Report URI, les sites de 178 entreprises et organisations ont été exposés à un malware ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, entre 5 h 21 du matin et 22 heures environ (heure de Paris). Parmi les sites compromis, nous pouvons notamment citer GitLab, Transavia, Air France-KLM, IKEA, ASOS, HSBC ou encore la plateforme de visioconférence Zoom. Pour être plus précis, ce ne sont pas les sites en eux-mêmes qui ont été compromis, mais un outil externe baptisé Optimizely, qui permet à ces sites de tester plusieurs versions de leurs pages web.
Un malware capable de voler des informations bancaires
Durant environ 15 heures, les sites web compromis ont chargé sans le savoir un malware. Les internautes de passage ont donc été exposés à ce malware durant ce laps de temps. Pour y parvenir, les pirates ont injecté des scripts JavaScript malveillants dans les projets de leurs clients, en passant par la plateforme Optimizely.
Le malware, défini par Report URI comme « un kit multifonctionnel », était capable de récupérer les cookies et les numéros de carte saisis dans les formulaires de paiement du site, mais aussi de remplacer les adresses des portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies par celles de l’attaquant. Il était également capable d’installer des kits d’exploitation sur des iPhone et des iPad non mis à jour. À noter toutefois que le malware n’aurait pas pu avoir accès aux paiements effectués via des modules externes comme Stripe ou Adyen.

articles.title: L'IA trouve les failles vraiment trop vite : Anthropic et Google sonnent la fin des 90 jours de grâce avant la divulgation
articles.summary:
Depuis des années, le milieu de la sécurité informatique suit une règle tacite : un chercheur qui trouve une faille prévient discrètement l’éditeur, puis lui laisse 90 jours avant de la rendre publique. Ce délai de trois mois doit permettre au correctif d’arriver chez tout le monde avant que les pirates ne connaissent la faille, et s’en servent.
Or, dans un billet publié ce lundi 16 novembre, Anthropic, l’entreprise derrière l’intelligence artificielle Claude, a décidé de ramener ce délai à 30 jours pour les failles de gravité élevée ou critique, et à 45 jours pour les autres. Les nouvelles règles valent pour les signalements faits à partir du 1er janvier 2027.
Et la raison profonde de ce bouleversement dans les principes de divulgation coordonnée et responsable ? L’IA.
Une faille ne reste plus secrète trois mois, estime Anthropic
Anthropic justifie ce changement par les progrès rapides des modèles d’IA, devenus bien meilleurs pour dénicher des failles. Selon l’entreprise, une brèche repérée par une IA a de plus en plus de chances d’être retrouvée par une autre, bien avant le délai des 90 jours, ce qui augmente fortement le degré de risque en sécurité informatique.

articles.title: Chrome 158 Patches 204 Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Google on Tuesday announced the release of Chrome 158 to the stable channel with patches for 204 vulnerabilities, including six critical-severity bugs.
The critical flaws include three use-after-free issues in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio, out-of-bounds write defects in GPU and ANGLE, and a buffer overflow in Media.
No bug bounty reward will be paid for any of these. In fact, no reward will be handed out for 163 of the security weaknesses. Google and Xinyang Ge discovered 145 and 15 of them, respectively.
Of the remaining vulnerabilities, 62 are high-severity issues, 82 are medium-severity, and 54 are low-severity.
Google says it handed out $11,000 in rewards for five of the vulnerabilities reported by external researchers and has yet to determine the amounts to be paid for 36 flaws.
The most common type of vulnerability patched in Chrome 158 is use-after-free (51 occurrences), followed by incorrect authorization (34), missing authorization (16), out-of-bounds write/read (15), uninitialized resource (14), information leak (11), UI misrepresentation (10), improper input validation (9), and race condition (8).
Google makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but users are advised to update their browsers as soon as possible.
The latest Chrome iteration is now rolling out as versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and macOS, and as version 158.0.8127.36 for Linux.

On November 17, 2026, the security research company Calif disclosed Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the most widely used Java runtime. The vulnerability lets a remote attacker with no credentials send malformed Base64 data to a Java application and overwrite memory next to the decoded output. Calif turned that overwrite into a leak of heap memory, similar to Heartbleed, and into remote code execution. Calif demonstrated pre-authentication remote code execution against Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations, and post-authentication remote code execution against Apache Kafka, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker.

articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Tackling GPU Bottlenecks in Plane-Wave DFT with K-Point Batching and Mixed Precision | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Training a next-generation machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) requires ground truth: tens to hundreds of millions of density functional theory (DFT) calculations of energies, forces, and stresses across diverse structures and chemistries.
Plane-wave DFT, with VASP as its dominant implementation, is the gold standard for generating that data. It is accurate, well-validated across materials classes, and ubiquitous at the national labs and research institutions running these calculations at scale.
As MLIP training datasets have grown, so has the pressure to generate DFT data faster and cheaper. But the small unit cells and dense k-point grids common in MLIP data generation can leave significant GPU performance unused. VASP’s OpenACC implementation has delivered meaningful speedups, especially for large-system calculations. However, for smaller systems, sequential k-point processing limits GPU utilization. At the same time, AI workloads are reshaping GPU hardware development toward lower-precision data types, creating a growing gap between what modern NVIDIA GPUs can deliver and what FP64-only HPC codes are optimized for.
This post introduces two new NVIDIA capabilities that address these bottlenecks. The first, Daviator, resolves the small-system GPU performance problem through k-point and spin-batched GPU kernels. In particular, a batched Davidson solver delivers significant performance gains. The second, a new mixed precision execution layer, enables further perform…

articles.title: Can AI Make Its Own Manufacturing Decisions?
articles.summary:
AI can optimize processes and find defects, but autonomous decisions require better data and strict process controls.
Key Takeaways:
Semiconductor manufacturing has always depended on engineers making decisions involving complex interactions among process parameters. An etch recipe, for example, may involve combinations of RF power, pressure, gas chemistry, temperature, and timing, each affecting multiple process characteristics. Changing one parameter might improve critical dimension control while creating problems elsewhere. But as devices and manufacturing processes become more complicated, the growing number of variables involved makes those decisions increasingly difficult.
AI-driven manufacturing offers a way to manage some of that complexity, from finding better process conditions to identifying defects and responding to problems on the production line. But how much production responsibility engineers are willing to give those systems remains an open question, and one that drew considerable attention at SEMICON West 2026.
“No matter how good we are as engineers, no matter how disciplined and objective we are, we tend to approach these difficult problems with historical biases,” said David Fried, chief AI officer and corporate vice president of Semiverse Solutions at Lam Research during a conference panel. “A process engineer might look at a set of data and say, ‘I need to move into a lower-pressure, higher-power regime because that’s how we solved this problem 10 years…

articles.title: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan and Bank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eighth largest bank, changed its terms today.

The first organization was hit in late 2025, using the compromised credentials of a super admin account. The APT leveraged a residential proxy network close to the victim and relied on multi-factor authentication (MFA) push notification fatigue to register a device to the victim’s tenant.

articles.title: Detachable Fiber Connectors Pose New Challenges For Photonics
articles.summary:
Multiple designs are emerging for CPO and NPO, but standardization and high-volume manufacturing are still not ready.
Key Takeaways:
As photonics shifts from pluggable optical transceivers toward near- and co-packaged optics (NPO, CPO), engineers are devising new ways to attach fibers to the photonics chips on a board. Several different designs exist today, but so far there is no common interface.
With pluggable photonics, lasers and connections are attached at the server faceplate, with the board itself housing only electronic components. Yet long electrical connections to the faceplate mean higher power and longer latency. Fibers would need to move onto the interior of the board to solve that. That eliminates the need for pluggables, but it requires new solutions.

Its purpose is to secure the AI tools and agents that are increasingly being adopted, used, and modified in-house by company employees. This is happening at pace and volume – so the object of ASE is a moving target; and is a security requirement that is different to and separate from cybersecurity.

Grand Theft Auto VI feels both refreshingly new and stuck in the past.
On the one hand, Rockstar’s long-running open-world crime franchise has finally grown up thanks to a more mature and emotionally-charged narrative. But on the other hand, some dated mechanics and mission design make the experience drag in places. Still, it’s a remarkable accomplishment that’s greater than the sum of its parts — the sort that certainly none but Rockstar could make.
Above all else, GTA VI succeeds on the strength of its leads. It’s a sweeping 60-hour Bonnie & Clyde-style epic that focuses on veteran-turned-drug runner Jason Duval and gig worker and recent inmate Lucia Caminos. Notably, the latter is the series’ first non-optional female protagonist, and she is every bit the star as Jason. In fact, she’s easily the more compelling of the two.
Where Jason can sometimes feel overly stoic and passive, Lucia is vivacious, determined and thoughtful. articles.title: Nuevo hito para la Voyager 1, el primer objeto humano a un día luz de la Tierra
articles.summary:
Casi 50 años después de su lanzamiento, la Voyager 1 continúa haciendo historia. La sonda espacial ha alcanzado un nuevo hito al convertirse en el primer objetivo construido por humanos en alcanzar una distancia de un día luz de la Tierra, ha confirmado la NASA.
Hoy, miércoles 18 de noviembre de 2026, la Voyager 1 logró este registro. El mismo se produjo a las 05:16, hora del Este de Estados Unidos; es decir, a las 11:16, hora peninsular española. Esto significa que el vehículo se encuentra a unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros de nuestro planeta.
La Voyager 1 ya era el objeto humano más alejado de la Tierra, pero con este nuevo récord agiganta todavía más su leyenda. Recordemos que la sonda se lanzó en 1977 y junto con Voyager 2, su hermana gemela, ha dedicado las últimas cinco décadas no solo a estudiar el sistema solar, sino también a navegar hacia los confines de lo desconocido. En 2012 ingresó en el espacio interestelar y actualmente sigue enviando datos que captura con los instrumentos que aún tiene encendidos.
¿Pero qué implica realmente que Voyager 1 esté a un día luz de distancia de la Tierra? El Laboratorio de Propulsión a Chorro de la NASA (JPL) ha publicado un breve vídeo explicándolo de modo sencillo. La agencia espacial estadounidense indica que una partícula de luz demora 24 horas en viajar unos 26.000 millones de kilómetros, la distancia a la que hoy se encuentra la Voyager 1.
Esto quiere decir que cualquier comando que se envíe desde la Tierra demora 24 horas …

It found that businesses making less than $3 million in annual revenue have a harder time improving their productivity, and that these businesses need to reach a certain size to be able to invest in tech and automation to benefit from economies of scale, BDC chief economist and vice president of research Pierre Cléroux told BetaKit in a Tuesday interview.

articles.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
articles.summary:
In the one light-day that humanity’s most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again.
Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter’s moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a “commemorative phonograph record,” in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.
About those forgotten bits, ask Glen Swanson. While researching the history of the Golden Record, he uncovered the discs’ overlooked second set of operating directions and located the duplicates that were made and distributed almost five decades ago.
“So much has been written about the contents of the record—the message in the bottle, so to speak—whereas I was more interested in the hardware, the bottle itself, because so very little is known about that,” Swanson, former chief historian for NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston and founding editor of Quest: The History of Spaceflight Quarterly, said in an interview.

articles.title: Windows 11 : pourquoi certaines de vos applications risquent bientôt de refuser de démarrer
articles.summary:
La sécurité dans Windows 11 est sur le point de subir une évolution majeure. Microsoft vient en effet d’introduire sa nouvelle Windows Baseline Protection, un nouveau système de protection qui laissera chaque application installée sur votre PC décider si votre configuration est suffisamment sécurisée pour qu’il puisse s’exécuter.
Un nouveau bilan de sécurité unique pour Windows
Concrètement, cette Windows Baseline Protection consiste à regrouper huit fonctionnalités de sécurité matérielle et logicielle du système sous la forme d’une simple vérification binaire. Contrairement au passé, où la sécurité d’un PC consistait à un assemblage d’options séparées qui devaient être vérifiées individuellement, ce nouvel outil, va regrouper huit modules de protection du système au sein d’un bilan de sécurité unique qui fournira un résultat simple.
Windows contrôlera alors votre puce TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, la sécurité basée sur la virtualisation (VBS), l’intégrité de la mémoire, la signature des pilotes (pour empêcher le chargement des pilotes de périphériques non identifiés), les pilotes certifiés Windows, la protection contre le débogage du noyau, et enfin le blocage des pilotes vulnérables.
Au démarrage de votre PC, tous ces éléments de sécurité seront ainsi vérifiés par Windows qui indiquera si « oui » ou « non » votre machine est correctement protégée.
Ce signal unique sera ensuite annoncé aux applications installées sur votre ordinateur qui pourront alors décider des mesures à prendre …

articles.title: What Is Driving Silicon Wafer Demand Recovery?
articles.summary:
The high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.
Global silicon wafer shipments are forecast to grow 11.8% in 2026, according to the Q3 2026 SEMI Silicon Wafer Market Monitor. This increase is primarily due to strong demand for AI, which is projected to drive shipments through 2029.
Alongside AI, rising process material sales are also supporting recovery. The positive correlation between material sales and silicon wafer demand not only reflects growth in manufacturing complexity, but it also points to greater material consumption per wafer.
Finally, increases in memory demand, precautionary inventory building, and global fab capacity expansions are boosting silicon wafer shipments as well.
To better understand today’s landscape, it’s helpful to revisit past silicon wafer demand curves. From 2018 to 2019 and from 2022 to 2023, silicon wafer shipments rose ahead of major increases in memory work-in-process (WIP) inventories, or unfinished memory chips undergoing fabrication. However, shipments lagged at the same time WIP inventory peaked. Because fabrication lines were already producing at full capacity, their need for silicon wafers slowed.
While this pattern provides historical context for today’s demand recovery, the high number of new and upcoming production lines is a unique factor influencing this particular cycle.

articles.title: Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
articles.summary:
Elon Musk said Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is lying about disruptions to Starshield in Ukraine and that he’s trying to misuse SpaceX’s consumer service, Starlink, for military purposes. Musk made the comments at The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday as he tried to explain the conflict following weeks of back and forth between Zelenskyy, Musk, and the US government.
Elon Musk tries to explain what’s going on with Ukraine and Starlink
The SpaceX CEO claims that Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy is ‘lying’ about using Starshield.
“From the beginning, I’ve said that Starlink is a civilian system,” Musk said. “It is not meant to be used for offensive drone strikes that kill people. If you want to do that, you need to do Starshield, which is a separate system that is controlled by the US government. But do not ask me as a private individual to make kill decisions.”
Musk also said that “if they want to do something that’s an offensive military action, it needs to be the Starshield system where the kill decision is that of the War Department, perhaps ultimately the president, and not mine.”
The interviewer, Andrew Ross Sorkin, said that President Zelenskyy refers to the system as Starshield and is claiming that is the system that was slowed down. “That’s false,” Musk said, claiming that Zelenskyy is “not always truthful.”

articles.title: TechCabal expands SA coverage with launch of TC Mzansi
articles.summary:
TechCabal is launching TC Mzansi, a weekly newsletter dedicated to South Africa’s technology and innovation economy, as the pan-African technology publication deepens its editorial presence in one of the continent’s largest technology markets.
Tomiwa Aladekomo, CEO of Big Cabal Media, TechCabal’s parent company, announced the newsletter at Africa Tech Festival in Cape Town on Wednesday. The first edition is scheduled to reach subscribers’ inboxes on November 23, extending the publication’s coverage of South Africa and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
The launch reflects TechCabal’s push to build a stronger regional newsroom presence and give South Africa’s technology industry more dedicated coverage. While the publication has reported on African technology for 13 years, starting in Lagos, Nigeria, it has expanded its operations in South Africa with a Johannesburg-based editorial team.
“We have hired an A-team here, and next week we’re launching a new newsletter focused on South Africa. It’s TC Mzansi,” Aladekomo said during a fireside chat moderated by Jessica Hope, founder and chief executive officer of public relations firm Wimbart.
He said the newsletter would focus on telling stories about innovation in South Africa, including the journey from university research and technological development to commercial products, as well as connecting the country’s technology ecosystem with the rest of the continent.

articles.title: Online shoppers can save $65 in fees at Rogers, Fido right now
articles.summary:
Rogers and flanker brand Fido are back to offering free shipping on phones as we head into the holiday shopping season. Moreover, Rogers is waiving its $40 device setup charge for online orders.
Previously, Rogers and Fido charged $25 for shipping. However, as of Nov. 17, both providers’ websites now list shipping costs as free. Further, a banner at the top of the websites notes that customers who buy online also skip the device setup fee.
It’s a notably change, both for the consumer savings as well as Rogers’ recent history with both these fees.
Rogers first launched the $25 shipping fee back in 2024 just ahead of that year’s iPhone launch. The fee stuck around for a while until it received some scrutiny from the CRTC earlier this year. Rogers briefly lowered the fee to $9 in July, only to increase it back to $25 in September.
The device setup fee, on the other hand, was a new charge Rogers introduced in response to the CRTC’s ban on junk fees. Rogers wasn’t the only one, with Bell also introducing a similar $40 device fee. The CRTC is still reviewing the fees to determine if the carriers violated the new rules.

articles.title: “Collaboration over competition”: Hugging Face hands model inference traffic to OpenRouter
articles.summary:
“Collaboration over competition”: Hugging Face hands model inference traffic to OpenRouter
Hugging Face and OpenRouter have announced a partnership that promises to make AI model inference faster and more reliable for developers.
The collaboration, announced by the two companies on Monday, will see Hugging Face use OpenRouter’s infrastructure to route language-model requests to third-party providers based on pricing, performance and reliability.
Previously, Hugging Face used its own routing system, introduced as part of its Inference Providers service in January 2025, to connect developers with companies running AI models. The service initially launched with four providers: Fal, Replicate, SambaNova and Together AI. The system would select a provider to handle each request, but if that provider encountered a problem, the request failed.
With OpenRouter now in the mix, the request can automatically be passed to another provider, meaning that developers should encounter fewer failed requests.
Hugging Face co-founder and CEO Clément Delangue sees the partnership as an example of how collaboration between AI companies can make open-weight models more accessible to developers, with each company focusing on its own strengths.
“Too many people treat AI as a zero-sum race. Open-source is winning by doing the opposite: collaboration over competition!”

articles.title: Google et Amazon vont détenir près d'un tiers d'Anthropic
articles.summary:
Amazon (14,7 %) et Google (13,7%) détiendront ensemble environ 28 % d’Anthropic après son introduction en Bourse, selon de nouveaux documents déposés auprès de la SEC. Une partie de ces titres vient de billets convertibles, et aucun ne donne de droit de vote. Anthropic et ses cofondateurs pourraient lever jusqu’à 64,4 milliards de dollars.
Anthropic doit fixer le prix de son action ce mercredi 18 novembre, avant une cotation jeudi sur le Nasdaq sous le symbole “ANT”. Les derniers documents d’Anthropic, repris par Bloomberg, précisent ce que deux de ses fournisseurs cloud vont détenir.
Actions sans vote et billets convertibles : comment Amazon et Google entrent au capital
Amazon et Google passent par une catégorie spéciale d’actions, la classe N. Ces titres ne donnent pas de voix en assemblée, seulement droit à d’éventuels dividendes. Amazon en recevra 1,92 milliard (34 % de la classe), soit 14,7 % d’Anthropic. Google en aura 1,79 milliard (32 % de la classe). Ses titres viennent à la fois d’une conversion de billets et du placement privé, où il a acheté 135,1 millions d’actions pour environ 10 milliards de dollars. Le poids des fondateurs n’est donc pas touché : Nous rapportions en fin de mois dernier que ces derniers garderaient 50,1 % des voix grâce à une action de classe F unique, détenue par Founder LLC.

articles.title: AI data centers delays push inference chips into existing sites - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Stalled data center buildouts send inference chips hunting for space in telco and colo sites
Demand for inference is outrunning the construction of new AI data centers, as power, capital and permitting delays push fresh capacity further out. That gap is sending chipmakers to hunt for room in existing facilities.
Many older telco and colocation sites have the space and power. But most can’t take today’s dense, liquid-cooled GPU racks without costly retrofits, which opens the door for air-cooled inference systems, according to Anton McGonnell (pictured), vice president of core product at SambaNova Systems Inc.
“We as an industry are just encumbered by the velocity of data center buildouts, and that’s been slowed down by just the physics of how long this takes, by the access to capital, and more and more by legislative hurdles — particularly in the U.S.,” McGonnell said.
McGonnell spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI data centers and the demand for air-cooled inference racks. (* Disclosure below.)
Reviving brownfield capacity for AI data centers
SambaNova’s fifth-generation chip, the SN50, targets the decode phase of inference, where output tokens are generated and data movement becomes the bottleneck. Microsoft has announced Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system, at the Ignite 2026 conference on Tuesday.
This new Windows Server version ships with a hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline that allows admins to relax specific settings.
"A hardened Server Core configuration by default and a new security baseline help reduce the work of establishing a secure baseline from day 1," said Neil Hinnant, Director of Windows Server & I/O Fabrics PM.
"Trusted Launch extends protection to virtual machines, guaranteeing boot integrity across your VM fleet, and Confidential VM support begins a journey to support integrity-protected runtimes on supported CVM hardware."

- Cryptography: TLS is limited to modern cipher suites, key exchange is hybrid post-quantum (ML-KEM), and stored keys are strongly protected.

articles.title: China threatens "countermeasures" on the face of new AI GPU rental and export restrictions — Beijing threatens retaliation ahead of Thursday's Xi Jinping meeting, Sino-American trade war may be renewed for a new season
articles.summary:
China threatens 'countermeasures' in the face of new AI GPU rental and export restrictions — Beijing threatens retaliation ahead of Thursday's Xi Jinping meeting, Sino-American trade war may be renewed for a new season
"When elephants fight, the grass suffers."
Yesterday, the Trump administration extended the reach of its existing export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips, namely, but not limited to, Nvidia's Blackwell lineup. The updated regulation now requires licenses for renting those chips in large quantities to the entirety of America's D:5 countries list (nations embargoed from arms sales). As expected, the news landed in Beijing like a lead dragon, and its Ministry of Commerce states that China "will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests."
The bold move taken by the U.S. arrives at a peculiar time, as President Trump is currently visiting the nation for the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Trump is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Nov. 19, a tête-a-tête that's bound to be interesting. Both nations were recently embroiled in a bitter trade war, with ever-mounting tariffs and restrictions on both sides until a temporary truce was called in Oct. 2025. Only some restrictions were lifted, though; for example, Chinese semiconductors still face a 50% tariff when imported stateside.

articles.title: PHP Readies Critical Security Updates to Patch Another RCE Flaw
articles.summary:
PHP is readying a new batch of critical security updates, four weeks after patches for the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities landed.
Scheduled for November 19, between 14:00 and 14:30 UTC, the refreshes will fix critical-severity issues that can be triggered in non-default configurations or uncommon setups.
“These releases are part of PHP’s regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions. The highest severity is Critical,” PHP’s maintainers noted in a pre-release announcement.
One of the security defects expected to be resolved is CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution (RCE) defect in the file-upload progress tracking functionality. The vulnerability was publicly disclosed two days after PHP2Shell made headlines.
PHP’s maintainers warned at the time that the security flaw can be triggered only under an unusual combination of configuration and code.
“An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled,” PHP said last month.
Noting that patches would be released as part of the regular update cycle, PHP developers recommended disabling session upload, a setting also listed as a mitigation for CVE-2026-109619, one of the two RCE bugs tracked as PHP2Shell.

articles.summary:
Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
- November 16, 2026
- Source:
- University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.

The business model raises questions about what people will actually get when they buy a Cybercab. “You’ll never really own the car,” says Ivan Drury, the director of insights at Edmunds. “It’s more like $30,000 to buy into a franchise.”

If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. Sin embargo, la mayor parte de la masa de nuestra galaxia está compuesta por la enigmática materia oscura, de modo que toda esa masa se quedaría fuera. La alternativa es analizar el movimiento de las estrellas del halo galáctico, ya que este está perturbado por la influencia gravitatoria del conjunto total de la galaxia. Hasta ahora, se habían hecho algunas estimaciones al respecto, pero contaban con un porcentaje de error bastante alto. Sin embargo, una nueva medición, llevada a cabo con datos de DESI y Gaia, ha aportado una cifra muchísimo más precisa.
El equipo perfecto. DESI (Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument) es una colaboración internacional que se encarga principalmente de cartografiar el Universo en 3D para estudiar la energía oscura. Entre sus instrumentos destacan los espectrógrafos, capaces de descomponer la luz proveniente de las estrellas y analizar tanto su composición como parte de su movimiento. Según el efecto Doppler, si la estrella se aleja de nosotros su espectro se desplaza hacia el rojo, mientras que si se acerca lo hace hacia el azul. Por su parte, Gaia es un telescopio europeo que mide con precisión las posiciones de las estrellas a lo largo de los años.

Pero la ingeniera hace una excepción con la calefacción por suelo radiante, que aconseja dejar encendida a una temperatura baja debido a su inercia térmica. Vamos, que este sistema tarda bastante en calentarse y también en perder el calor que ha acumulado, de modo que no se puede regular igual que unos radiadores convencionales.

articles.title: Why verification, not generation, is your secret to AI coding ROI

Why verification, not generation, is your secret to AI coding ROI
For two years, the question around AI coding was whether agents could write good code. Developers have largely answered it: AI now generates or significantly assists 65% of the code they commit, according to Sonar’s 2027 State of Code Developer Survey. A year ago that figure was 42%, and this year’s number matches what respondents then expected to see a year later. Clearly, adoption is outrunning expectations.
“Clearly, adoption is outrunning expectations.”
This is because AI tools are getting better at coding, as shown by the increase in effectiveness our survey respondents (1,026 developers and engineering managers) reported alongside their increased adoption. The harder question is whether teams can trust what the agents ship. For most respondents, the report suggests the answer is “not quite yet,” but things are moving in the right direction.
The verification gap
Four numbers describe the problem:
- 53% spend more time reviewing code than creating it, compared to 18% before adopting AI tools.
- Despite this, 76% can’t verify code as fast as AI generates it
- 94% don’t fully trust that AI-generated code is functionally correct.
- However, only 39% always check AI-generated code before committing it, down from 48% last year.
As adoption of coding agents continues to increase, this is now happening in systems that matter. Seventy-six percent say their team or company uses AI coding tools for business-critical …

articles.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Apache has released security updates to address a critical Roller flaw that threat actors are exploiting to gain code execution on vulnerable servers.
Apache Roller is an open-source, Java-based group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than modern content management systems and blogging platforms.
However, while this is a niche product, Apache has flagged the flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-129448) as actively exploited in the wild.
Apache has not yet provided details about these ongoing attacks, including who is responsible and how many servers have already been compromised.
"Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester," Apache explained in a Tuesday security advisory.
"This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited."
To block ongoing attacks, Roller users should immediately upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects malicious XML-RPC requests after turning off the XML-RPC feature.
Admins who can't immediately upgrade can also temporarily mitigate CVE-2026-129448 by setting "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, removing the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restarting Roller.

Rapid root-cause identification of these systemic defects is critical to quickly improving yield and accelerating time-to-market.1 But conventional failure analysis relies heavily on wafer experimentation and statistical analysis, which can be slow and costly as manufacturing complexity increases.
That’s where calibrated virtual twins and machine-learning optimization can help.

articles.title: Waymo has stopped its robotaxis from driving on the freeway—here’s why

Waymo is currently restricting its fleet of robotaxis to surface streets after getting into hot water with California over its cars’ driving behavior on highways. Specifically, the software tends to drive into construction zones at speed. As first reported by the San Francisco Business Times, this behavior actually drew the ire of California’s DMV earlier this month, which ordered Waymo to stop driving on Californian highways immediately and until it can convince the DMV that its cars no longer “pose an imminent hazard to public safety.”
This is not Waymo’s first run-in with this problem. In Arizona, Waymo robotaxis did not recognize ramp closure signs on six occasions in Phoenix in April and entered construction zones. A month later in California, seven Waymo robotaxis entered lanes with active construction. In June, Waymo recalled the almost 3,800 robotaxis capable of highway driving. That problem led Waymo to stick to surface streets only in California after the May incidents until late July, when the robotaxis resumed highway operations.
In early July, Waymo told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration that it began updating the robotaxi software to a version that “improve[s] the recognition of freeway construction zones, more appropriately prioritize[s] construction zones over other freeway hazards, and reduce[s] speed when the AV detects that it may be in a construction zone.”

articles.title: S3 vs. ScyllaDB for tiny telemetry: What Red Canary learned the hard way

S3 vs. ScyllaDB for tiny telemetry: What Red Canary learned the hard way
At Red Canary, storing large amounts of small data is a big deal.
Their Linux Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) sensors run on hundreds of thousands of endpoints (VMs, laptops, EC2 instances, etc.) They continuously generate small payloads with telemetry details (file changes, process launches, and network connections), as well as self-reported health checks. Uploading all these small payloads to S3, which charges per PUT operation, became quite costly at scale.
The logical approach – merging data into larger chunks before uploading them to S3 — did cut costs. However, it also introduced file-size limits, delayed data freshness, and complicated debugging of specific endpoint records. After some experimentation, they cut latency and costs with an unexpected approach: storing large amounts of small data in a write-optimized database, ScyllaDB.

Limpiar la lavadora por dentro cada uno o dos meses, o después de unos 30 lavados, ayuda a eliminar residuos de detergente, humedad y pelusas que pueden afectar el lavado de la ropa.
Fabricantes como LG, Samsung y Whirlpool plantean esta frecuencia como una guía para conservar el equipo y prevenir problemas de olor, drenaje o acumulación de suciedad.
El mantenimiento no se limita a una limpieza programada. Después de cada uso, dejar la puerta abierta y retirar restos visibles de jabón o suavizante reduce la humedad dentro del tambor y evita que los residuos se adhieran a la goma, al dispensador o a los conductos. Estas acciones toman pocos minutos y ayudan a revisar el estado del aparato.
Los residuos se acumulan en partes que el ciclo de lavado no limpia
La lavadora usa agua y detergente para tratar las prendas, pero ese proceso no elimina todos los restos que quedan en el interior. Fibras textiles, suciedad, producto sobrante y humedad pueden concentrarse en áreas que no están a la vista.
Con el tiempo, esa mezcla puede provocar malos olores, manchas en la ropa, dificultades para evacuar el agua y obstrucciones. El problema suele aparecer en la junta de goma, el cajón del detergente y el filtro de drenaje, tres zonas que requieren revisiones regulares.

articles.title: Juan Manuel Rojas, arquitecto: “Si hoy tuviésemos albañiles como los que hicieron la Plaza de España, yo diseñaría una plaza así”

Con ello justifica que hay que llevar las viviendas a la fábrica.
El arquitecto fundó en 2002 su propio estudio Hombre de Piedra Arquitectos junto a Laura Domínguez. Además, es profesor en la Escuela Técnica Superior de Arquitectura de Sevilla. Pertenece a Arquitectura Industrializada Colaborativa (AIC), que es el grupo de trabajo de los colegios sevillanos de arquitectos y de arquitectura técnica que están trabajando en la industrialización de la construcción.
Para Rojas, hay que ver cómo era la albañilería de antes. Era un tipo de albañil que tenía un conocimiento muy grande. Recordemos al maestro que hacía el muro sin que el arquitecto le dijera mucho. Tenía un conocimiento que le permitía solucionar casi todo mejor que el arquitecto que proyectaba. Ahora, según él, tenemos un problema de falta de cualificación que pone en riesgo lo que pasa en las obras.
Rojas lo relaciona con el poco valor que se da al trabajo manual. También es un problema de remuneración de esa tarea. Antes se tenía más orgullo en hacer las cosas bien. Había un conocimiento que se pasaba de padres a hijos.

Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies, including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions.
“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey said onstage at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. Luckey disagrees with Huang’s longstanding position that Nvidia should have more leeway to export chips to China. But he also recognizes that China stands to benefit if its domestic chipmakers can challenge Nvidia’s dominance.
“China doesn’t want Nvidia to sell GPUs to Chinese companies,” Luckey said. “There are Chinese companies that want to buy Nvidia GPUs… China will not give them an import permit because they want to build an internal domestic processor industry… not build one that is dependent on the United States.”

articles.title: Starburst adds context support to give AI agents consistent access to business data definitions - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Starburst adds context support to give AI agents consistent access to business data definitions
Starburst Data Inc. is expanding its data federation platform into business context management with the introduction of Context Studio, a new capability designed to help artificial intelligence agents produce more accurate and trustworthy answers from information distributed across enterprise systems.
Context Studio collects business definitions from existing data catalogs, business intelligence tools, metric stores and documents, making them available alongside data when AI agents respond to prompts. The system is intended to eliminate conflicting definitions that can cause AI agents to produce incorrect results.
The new capability addresses a problem the company encountered as customers began deploying its Aida natural-language data assistant in production environments, said Starburst co-founder and Chief Executive Justin Borgman.
“We’ve found that as you get into production, the biggest issue is context because you need to trust the answers the agent gives back,” he said.
The challenge is particularly acute in large organizations where different departments may use different definitions of common business metrics, such as revenue or active customers. Without a consistent understanding of those terms, AI models can produce plausible but inaccurate answers.
“When those definitions conflict, the [large language model] doesn’t know any better; it’s just going to guess,” Borgman said…

Universities racing to build AI infrastructure are learning that raw compute changes the pace of science itself, from molecular discovery to materials engineering.

articles.title: Yelp Migrates Cassandra to EKS by Moving EBS Volumes
articles.summary:
Yelp has moved its Cassandra fleet from legacy self-managed Kubernetes clusters to Amazon EKS by re-pointing existing EBS volumes at new pods, rather than streaming data between nodes. A blog post by the site reliability team details a migration. It covered about 90 production clusters. There was zero downtime for customers and no data loss. The largest cluster, a 54-pod user-data store, took about 12 hours end to end.
Yelp had already moved its stateless workloads to EKS through its PaaSTA deployment layer, but Cassandra stayed behind. Kubernetes has no built-in way to migrate StatefulSets and their persistent volumes across clusters. The usual approach is to add nodes to the new cluster and shut down the old ones. This would temporarily double compute capacity but also lead to data transfer costs. For the largest clusters, streaming alone could have taken weeks. Yelp also considered a regional failover and rebuild, and a new Cassandra datacenter in EKS, but rated both as less transparent to customers.
Yelp's "Rolling PV Transplant" relies on the fact that an EBS volume is bound to an Availability Zone, not to a Kubernetes cluster, and that a PersistentVolume is effectively a pointer to a volume ID. The team pre-creates PVs and PVCs in EKS that reference the existing volume IDs, then creates an identical StatefulSet there, whose pods wait in ContainerCreating. As for how it happened, Optimizely told Gizmodo that someone exploited a vulnerability in its Experimentation account signup flow. The attacker then wrote code into each customer's "Project JavaScript" field. That setting runs on every page, so Optimizely's servers delivered the malware just like any legitimate experiment.

Key Takeaways:
Power delivery is now a significant performance limiter in data center chips. The demands of AI and high-performance computing chips running near 0.7 V for a 600W GPU are forcing current to rise to 1,000 amps and beyond, compounding resistive losses and voltage droop across the PDN. Multi-chiplet constructions only compound these issues by further increasing current density and signal congestion.
To solve these challenges, designers are turning to vertical power delivery networks, where the voltage regulator modules are relocated much closer to the processors from their position on the device periphery — to the PCB landside (under the PCB), inside the accelerator package, or inside the silicon interposer. Together with the growing customization of AI accelerator modules, there are many approaches on offer with varying design and manufacturing complexity.
The vertical PDN trend began nearly a decade ago with the integration of backside power delivery networks (BPDNs) on the wafer backside, enabling fine-tuned power delivery more directly to the transistors while reducing IR drop across the tens of interconnect levels on-chip. articles.title: Beyond Pass/Fail: Characterizing Silicon Margin With PVTW
articles.summary:
Determining not only whether a device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary, helps inform product robustness and future design decisions.
Production test is necessarily built around decisions. PASS. FAIL. Bin 1. Bin 2. Ship. Do not ship. Characterization has a different objective. It asks not only whether the device meets specification, but how far it is from the boundary.
That distinction becomes increasingly important as processors integrate compute, memory, high speed interfaces, multiple power domains and advanced packaging into increasingly complex systems.
Suppose five devices all pass the product specification, but under the same controlled workload their minimum stable operating voltages are:
0.70 V | 0.71 V | 0.73 V | 0.76 V | 0.79 V
Production test sees five passing devices. Characterization sees five different levels of margin. That changes the engineering question from “Why did this device fail?” to something potentially much more useful:
What is consuming product margin?
PVTW (process, voltage, temperature, workload) gives us a framework for exploring that question.
Take the same device and establish its voltage and frequency boundary using conventional ATE content. Then establish another boundary while running a deterministic compute workload. Repeat with SRAM, memory, PCIe and combined workloads. We may discover that the boundaries are different.

The provider shares a CIDR-type resource configuration through AWS Resource Access Manager and the consumer creates a tunnel endpoint against it. From then on, anything inside the range is reachable, including resources that did not exist when the share was made.
Bruce Pinsky and Ashish Kumar of AWS frame it as a vendor-access problem, for "a vendor or service provider whose software must reach applications and resources in a customer's network." Until now, that meant a separate PrivateLink resource configuration per database or host, which breaks down when the resources are ephemeral, or the customer does not want to enumerate them. With a CIDR configuration, the customer defines a perimeter in address ranges, and "resources located outside the perimeter can't be reached by the vendor." Two further properties come with the design: the consumer and provider VPCs can use overlapping CIDR blocks, and connections "can start only from the consumer VPC, not from the provider network."
(Source: AWS Networking & Content Delivery blog)

Cuando el presentador le preguntó si seguiremos necesitando a los humanos, contestó que no para la mayoría de las cosas, pero añadió que eso lo decidiremos nosotros: “Como el béisbol. La IA como acelerador. En las otras tres áreas, la tecnología haría de acelerador más que de sustituto. articles.title: Microsoft’s Agent Framework PyPI package compromised to steal credentials
articles.summary:
Hackers compromised Microsoft's official Agent Framework Python package on PyPI, publishing two malicious versions designed to steal cloud credentials and other sensitive information from developers' systems.
Microsoft Agent Framework is Microsoft's open-source toolkit for building AI agents and coordinating them in workflows. It's a fairly popular tool with roughly 200,000 monthly downloads on PyPI.
The malicious releases, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published on November 17, 2026, and contained a credential stealer that executed automatically during normal Python startup in affected environments, even when the Agent Framework package was not imported.
Both versions retained their dependency on the legitimate agent-framework-core 1.26.0 package, allowing the framework to function normally while the malware ran in the background.
Multiple security firms discovered and documented the attack, including Socket, Step Security, and Ox Security.
Version 1.26.1 contained a credential stealer that harvested secrets from environment variables, local configuration files, and other running processes where permissions allowed, targeting Azure, AWS, GitHub, Docker, Hugging Face, OpenAI, and other services.
The malware also attempted to obtain Azure managed identity access tokens and Azure DevOps OIDC tokens, potentially giving attackers access to additional cloud resources.
Version 1.26.2 added GitHub Actions OIDC token requests and searches of GitHub runner directories.

The gap between a web form lead and a fully qualified lead is significant. Bankruptcy attorneys place more value on a lead that includes detailed financial data: debts, assets, vehicles, real estate, employment history, and prior filings. The web form could have been extended to capture that detail, but the longer it got, the more visitors abandoned it partway through. A phone interview would have drawn the information out naturally, because people are more willing to share financially sensitive details in conversation, but staffing and training a human intake team to run those interviews was cost-prohibitive.

articles.title: Si tienes una tarjeta NVIDIA, este error oculto podría estar dañando tu SSD sin que lo notes

Un fallo en los controladores de NVIDIA podría estár desgastando los SSD en Windows. Una serie de reportes en los foros de NVIDIA y Dell afirman que algunas versiones de los drivers de GeForce realizan escrituras constantes en el disco, incluso cuando el ordenador permanece inactivo. El ciertas condiciones, el controlador escribe más de 500 MB de datos en apenas cinco minutos.
De acuerdo con Neowin, la alerta surgió luego de que se detectara un problema similar con los drivers de AMD. Varios usuarios con una tarjeta gráfica de NVIDIA detectaron un comportamiento anómalo con el archivo nvlog.nvlgstg, el cual utilizan los componentes de registro y telemetría. Según los reportes, este archivo se reescribe continuamente por el proceso NVDisplay.Container.exe, lo que significa que tu SSD trabaja más de la cuenta.
En un hilo de soporte en los foros de NVIDIA, un usuario reveló que el controlador GRD 621.14 escribió 512 MB de datos en cinco minutos, algo que no ocurría con la versión 621.01:
"NVDisplay.Container.exe reescribe continuamente el archivo de registro binario en C:\ProgramData\NVIDIA Corporation\nvtopps\nct\nvlog.nvlgstg, lo que provoca escrituras pesadas en SSD mientras el PC está inactivo", mencionó en su publicación. "El Monitor de Recursos mostraba NVDisplay.Container.exe escribiendo entre 4,6 y 5,2 MB/s en este archivo, sin que ningún juego se ejecutara".

Applications are now open for the Spring 2027 cohort of the Kora Collective, a private network for seed-to-Series A founders building for emerging markets.
The Kora Collective is aimed at founders who are past day zero, have found traction, and are now focused on scaling, whether through bigger teams, new markets or better products. Its members are backed by investors including Coinbase, Digital Currency Group, Kraken, Hustle Fund, Jump and Cadenza.
The Spring 2027 cohort will bring together 15 founders, and will kick off in London in April. Members are placed in a small peer group of founders at a similar stage and in the same vertical across markets, and are paired with a coach.
They also take part in off-the-record sessions with operators who have built category-defining companies, reached US$1 billion-plus valuations and exited, and are connected one-on-one with senior venture capitalists matched to them based on fit.
For now, the collective is focused on two areas – payments and money movement, and credit, but an artificial intelligence (AI) track, covering agents, automation and intelligent infrastructure, is set to be added in future.
According to the Kora Collective, its existing members have processed more than US2.7 billion in combined volume, raised an average of US$6 million, and serve more than 10 countries across Africa, Asia and Latin America.

articles.title: Tesorai raises $5.3M to feed starving AI models with biological data and accelerate drug discovery - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Tesorai raises $5.3M to feed starving AI models with biological data and accelerate drug discovery
Drug researchers and medical laboratories generate massive volumes of biological data every single day, yet somehow the artificial intelligence models designed to speed up drug discovery are still starved of useful information.
It’s a strange paradox, but a startup called Tesorai Inc. believes it has the solution after raising $5.3 million in seed funding today.
The round included Perplexity Fund, IQT, South Central Ventures, New Stack Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, f7 Ventures, VitalStage Ventures and ZAKA participating. With its completion, Tesorai has now raised $8 million in total, and will use that money to try to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery by digging deeper into existing datasets to surface the deeply buried insights that human researchers have missed.
Biological data covers a broad spectrum spanning genetic sequences to protein measurements, and metabolomic processes to cellular imaging. This information is extremely valuable to drug researchers, because it serves as the primary fuel for training advanced AI models that can predict disease pathways and identify new therapies.
AI-accelerated drug discovery is seen as one of the most promising use cases for this technology, but it hasn’t yet managed to change the world in the same way that generative AI has done. Why not? Because researchers still don’t have nearly enough of it, which limits the accuracy…

articles.title: Will Wright's next simulation will use AI to mine content from your memories
articles.summary:
The computer gaming world hasn’t heard much from Will Wright (SimCity, The Sims) since the underwhelming release of Spore in 2008 and Wright’s subsequent departure from Maxis owner EA. Now, well over 15 years later, Wright is starting to promote his next digital simulation, which will use generative AI technology to craft a game-like experience from players’ memories.
MyMems, which is slated to release next year, differentiates itself from Wright’s previous projects by “turn[ing] the simulation inward,” as Wright’s Gallium Studios and partner Artificial Agency put it in a press release this morning. The game will mine memories provided by the player to create digital people that can then form teams to solve puzzles in the game world.
“If my Grandmother ended up in a Grand Slam match against Serena Williams, who would win?” Wright says by way of example in the release. “If I had to build a bridge across a short chasm, which three people from my life would I choose to help me?”
In an accompanying announcement video, Wright talks about how the “plausible behavior” in a game like The Sims still didn’t effectively capture the nuances of people he encounters in real life. “It was nowhere near them understanding my claustrophobia or why my sister and I fought so much… We’re actually taking parts of your life, your memories, your experiences, people you know, and turning that into a game that’s very personal.”
Wright said MyMems will be able to extract generalized themes from your me…

articles.title: Na era da IA, audiência do Reddit despenca 13% • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Na era da IA, audiência do Reddit despenca 13%
Fórum é uma das principais fontes de consulta dos modelos de inteligência artificial atuais, inclusive o Gemini, que entrega os resumos na página de busca.
O Reddit é mais uma “vítima” da ausência de cliques por conta dos resumos de IA: o fórum perdeu 13% da audiência no último ano. Apesar disso, em carta enviada para acionistas, a empresa afirma que viu o número de acessos únicos subir 16% no mesmo período.
O site é uma das principais fontes online utilizadas por modelos de IA generativa para gerar suas respostas, assim como outras redes sociais e o Wikipédia. A própria Wiki também já perdeu acessos recentemente, segundo levantamento feito em setembro.
Vale lembrar que o Reddit passou a exigir login após 20 anos aberto. O motivo seria, justamente, a facilidade de acesso do Gemini para extrair dados e gerar seus resumos. A queda registrada pela pesquisa da Similarweb, entretanto, leva em conta um período anterior à nova medida.
Esse número menor de cliques nas páginas do Reddit não chega a ser novidade. Outros sites, sobretudo aqueles que publicam conteúdo escrito, também vêm sofrendo com a IA do Google. A empresa estadunidense, inclusive, já sofreu alguns processos na justiça dos Estados Unidos por utilizar informações de maneira gratuita e sem nenhum retorno para quem as produz.
Até o momento, nenhuma dessas ações levou a uma derrota judicial especificamente relacinada ao tema. Ainda assim, um juiz de Washington reconheceu o pr…

articles.title: European game dev unions publish a manifesto calling on studios to ditch generative AI
articles.summary:
What just happened? Use of generative AI in game development is now widespread and controversial. As tech giants promote the productivity gains the technology supposedly offers, developers and users debate its usefulness, impact, and ethics. Several European game development unions have recently come out flatly against GenAI, summarizing every major criticism of the technology, including its environmental impact, accusations of stolen material, its cognitive effects on workers and employers, and more.
Unions representing game developers in the United Kingdom, Ireland, Spain, and Italy recently published a lengthy manifesto calling on companies to abandon or at least carefully monitor GenAI use. The document cites numerous studies on the technology's negative impacts in different sectors of the workforce.
Interestingly, the manifesto's section on using human input to train AI without consent is its smallest, but the unions stress that this doesn't diminish its importance. The AI industry has previously admitted that the technology can't exist without copyright infringement, and a Microsoft executive even called it the largest labor theft in human history.
The manifesto also alleges that many workers are being implicitly and explicitly forced to use GenAI, which shouldn't be necessary if it always saves time and increases productivity. Instead, the unions cite studies saying that the technology makes tasks more monotonous and causes skills to atrophy.

articles.title: Vercel Releases UI SDK for Agents to Compose UI from Reusable Behaviors
articles.summary:
Vercel has released UI SDK, an open-source TypeScript library that treats keyboard navigation, focus, selection, popups, and drag and drop as reusable behaviors rather than details buried inside finished components. Vercel UI SDK is published on GitHub as vercel-labs/ui and is currently in beta.
The behaviors live in @ui-sdk/core. Vercel says it built more than 50 of them, including createPopup, createSelection, createTypeahead, createRovingFocus, createReorder, createResize, createViewport, createListbox, createChange, createFocusRecovery, and createVirtualizer. A developer, or more often an agent, combines those helpers inside definePrimitive, which declares a component's state, API, and slots once. Framework adapters then render the same primitive through createParts in React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, or as Web Components. The parts are unstyled and expose attributes and CSS variables. The same behaviors also back a starter library of more than 50 unstyled components, from Color Picker, Token Input, and Command to Calendar, Tree, and OTP Input, with the same part names in all five adapters.
UI SDK is meant to be used by agents, not only written by them. The ui-sdk skill, installed with npx skills add vercel-labs/ui --skill ui-sdk, points an agent at the Markdown docs shipped in the installed packages. At runtime, createAgent, imported from the matching framework package such as @ui-sdk/react/agent, exposes snapshot, act, and query so an agent can read component state and call a…

articles.title: One GPU, 10 minutes, hundreds of millions of vectors: The math reshaping AI search
articles.summary:
AI needs fresh data. Vector indexing is getting in the way
It’s not a revelation to say AI workflows are changing enterprise infrastructure. What gets less attention, though, is how they’re also shifting the fundamentals of data processing and search.
The complication lies in the data. As organizations build generative AI (GenAI) applications, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, and AI agents, they’re generating an unwieldy number of vectors from growing volumes of unstructured data. And with all that vectorized data comes a challenge: how to quickly find the right information to power AI applications and workflows.
“After all, a model can only reason over the context you can find and feed it.”
Whether it’s a RAG system answering a question or an AI agent taking action, enterprise AI applications succeed on retrieval. After all, a model can only reason over the context you can find and feed it. If those systems rely on wrong or outdated information, even the best model can’t fix the underlying context problem.
But finding the right context inside petabytes of enterprise data is a difficult search problem — one keyword search alone is no match.
Search has moved beyond keywords
In recent years, search has come a long way from basic keyword-based matching. For one, user behavior has spearheaded a push from simple keyword entries to natural language queries. Agent workloads, meanwhile, which query 10 to 100 times more than humans, bring a new dimension to search — and t…

articles.summary:

articles.title: Data breach impacts 40 Irish credit unions in reported IT provider hack
articles.summary:
A reported cyberattack on Wellington IT has exposed sensitive information belonging to members of 50 credit unions, the majority of which are located in Ireland.
Wellington IT is a Belfast-based supplier whose services are used by about 50 credit unions, including 43 in Ireland.
While the company has not publicly disclosed a security incident, Minister of State Robert Troy confirmed to RTÉ that Wellington IT is the third-party service provider linked to the cybersecurity incident involving credit unions, resulting in the exposure of data from about 40 credit unions in Ireland.
The company reportedly notified affected organizations of a data breach that posed a risk of financial fraud, impersonation, and targeted phishing to their members.
According to the Irish Examiner, which saw the notices, Wellington IT informed customers that an automated script made five million requests to exploit an authorization flaw in the company's infrastructure.
The attack unfolded between October 2 and 4, 2026, and the attacker accessed private records using valid credentials.
However, the firm said it lacked activity logs that would specify which member data was compromised and therefore cannot verify the impact on individual payees.
Minister R. Troy characterized the massive delay in Wellington IT notifying the credit unions as "not acceptable."
At this time, the total number of impacted individuals is unknown.

Bajaj Finance and Pennant Technologies are backing Soket AI with investments of around $2 million each to advance its homegrown foundation models and enterprise AI solutions.
A bank may want to use AI, but can it trust the technology with sensitive customer data?

articles.title: Blutzucker messen ohne Nadel: Dieser Zahnseidestick analysiert Flüssigkeit am Zahnfleisch
articles.summary:
Statt Pikser in den Finger: Mikrofluidik-Zahnseide misst Glukose und Harnsäure im Mund
Ein Team der Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) sowie der University of Hong Kong (HKU) in der gleichnamigen chinesischen Sonderverwaltungszone hat ein Analysegerät in Form eines Zahnseidesticks entwickelt. Wie aus einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin „Science Advances“ veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, sammelt das unter der Leitung der Chemieingenieurin Hnin Yin Yin Nyein konstruierte „Gingival Fluid Device“ (GFD) winzige Flüssigkeitsmengen aus der Zahnfleischfurche und wertet sie direkt im Handstück elektrochemisch aus.
Innerhalb von drei Minuten ermittelt das System vier Biomarker: Glukose, Harnsäure, Wasserstoffperoxid sowie den pH‑Wert. Anders als Speichel, der durch Nahrung, Getränke und schwankende Produktionsmengen stark verdünnt wird, stammt die sogenannte gingivale Sulkusflüssigkeit aus dem Blutserum und spiegelt sowohl den systemischen Stoffwechsel als auch lokale Entzündungen im Mundraum wider.
