Für Menschen mit chronischen Stoffwechselerkrankungen wie Diabetes mellitus besteht ein direkter Zusammenhang zwischen Blutzuckerwerten und der Mundgesundheit, da ihr Risiko für eine Parodontitis dreimal so hoch ist wie in der Allgemeinbevölkerung. In many enterprises, a central network team owns every virtual private cloud (VPC) and subnet, and every flow between VPCs must pass a central firewall in both directions. articles.title: Nigeria’s Payaza secures Central Bank of Kenya licence - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Nigerian payments infrastructure company Payaza has been authorised by the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to provide payment gateway services, just weeks after getting regulatory approval in Zambia.
Payaza offers payment collection, payout and merchant tools to businesses in Africa and international markets. It handles card, mobile money and bank payments in more than 40 currencies and operates in more than 27 countries.
The CBK approval allows Payaza to operate as a licensed payment service provider in Kenya. It can now serve local merchants directly with online checkout and payment acceptance. The licence does not cover deposit-taking or customer wallets.
It comes after the Bank of Zambia gave Payaza a Certificate of Designation of a Payment System. The company has also recently picked up payment licensing milestones in China, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
“Kenya is the heartbeat of East Africa’s digital economy, and we are entering it the right way: fully licensed,” said Seyi Ebenezer, Payaza’s group CEO. “Coming so soon after our Bank of Zambia approval, this licence from the Central Bank of Kenya connects East, West and Southern Africa on one regulated platform.”
Payaza says it will now speed up merchant onboarding, build closer ties with banks and mobile money operators, and seek more licences across Africa, especially in East Africa. Nigeria makes up about 35 per cent of its revenue.

articles.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83 a share, above projected range | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Anthropic has priced its long-awaited IPO at $83 per share, above its initial range of $70 to $78, signaling strong investor appetite for one of the companies at the center of the AI boom, despite market jitters following the departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, which shook confidence in the industry. Most campaigns begin with the same video discovery problem: finding the one moment in the footage that will resonate with an audience. When a brief lands, the clock starts, and what they need is almost never something a database can describe.
Semantic search, on its own, has a ceiling: It answers the question you can articulate. Ask it for a character holding a coffee mug and it will find every coffee mug in a thousand episodes. The queries that actually drive entertainment campaigns look nothing like that. They are questions of judgment: which moment in a show will travel, which line is quotable, and which single frame will work as a meme.
Those questions can’t be typed into a search box. Answering them requires two things the search index doesn’t have: an editorial definition of what “quotable” or “memeable” means for a given library, and a continuously refreshed view of what is moving outside the library. Historically, answering them meant a person with deep knowledge of the show watching footage for a week, and that person doesn’t scale across a catalog.

International health authorities formally announced on Tuesday that the US has lost its measles elimination status, a hard-fought public health triumph won in 2000 after decades-long vaccination efforts. The loss had been widely expected by public health experts for months, and the decision was leaked by the press last week. Still, having the designation officially stripped stings.
After the announcement Tuesday, public health experts, doctors, and political leaders decried the dramatic backslide for the US, calling it “shameful” and a “national embarrassment.” News articles point to the staggering vertical rise of measles cases this year, currently over 5,400 cases, more than any other year since 1991. An explosive measles outbreak in Pennsylvania accounts for over 1,500 of those cases. There have been 10 confirmed deaths across three states, several deaths just in the last week.
But the measles data that caused the US to lose its status—the bits of it that are public at least—paint a darker picture of where the US is in its rematch with measles, the most contagious virus known on Earth. For one thing, almost none of the data from this year—the cases, the explosive Pennsylvania outbreak, the deaths—factored in to the loss. It was lost earlier. What’s happening now is a runaway epidemic.

Coinbase says it blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to scammers promoting a fake giveaway using an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream that attracted more than 500,000 viewers.
The deepfake took place during Tesla's "flying car" demonstration, when scammers created a fake YouTube livestream that appeared to broadcast the event.
The fraudulent stream featured an AI-generated video of Musk, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and a QR code, promising viewers that any cryptocurrency they sent would be doubled.
According to Coinbase, hundreds of its customers attempted to send millions of dollars to the scammers over about two hours, including many longtime users of the exchange.
However, the company says its AI-powered fraud-prevention systems detected the scam and blocked about 91% of the attempted transfers, totaling $4.7 million.
Unlike traditional cryptocurrency theft involving compromised accounts or stolen credentials, victims in this campaign voluntarily made the crypto transfer after believing the livestream was real.
Coinbase explained that this makes scams like these difficult to detect because the transactions are created and approved by legitimate account holders.
"Most fraud defenses are built to spot activity the customer didn't authorize," Coinbase explained.
"That's not what happened here. The customer was logged in, the customer pressed confirm, and the customer believed it was the opportunity of a lifetime."

Pour être valable dans les 27 pays, l’autorisation doit encore passer par un vote du TCMV, le comité technique où siègent les États membres, à la majorité qualifiée : au moins 15 pays représentant 65 % de la population.

Le poids de Paris compte, parce que sans la France et l’Allemagne, qui pèsent à elles deux environ un tiers de la population de l’UE, le seuil de 65 % deviendrait presque impossible à atteindre.

Speaking at The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, the tech executive argued that the shift to an agentic web could change which companies pay others for traffic and for transactions, similar to how the transition from web portals like Yahoo to search engines like Google did years ago.
“The current aggregators who have a business model which was for the human web will get, in some sense, reshuffled,” said Nadella. “And if you were monetizing ads because of the eyeballs, you now have to probably get down to essentially maybe CPC [cost-per-click] wins; maybe it’s more transactional,” he continued. “And so if you don’t accept the agent, somebody else will.”
The discussion turned to Amazon and its decision to block AI agents from accessing its retail website, preventing them from browsing its catalog and making purchases on behalf of their users. Nadella suggested that companies trying to protect their existing business models could lose out to others that are more willing to embrace the AI agents. Quantum computing drops its decade-away tag as error rates fall 200-fold in two years
Quantum computing is shedding its reputation as speculative as gains in quantum error correction turn fragile machines into reliable ones. For the supercomputing community, which now measures data centers in gigawatts of power, the more pressing question is how quantum fits beside the processors already on the floor.
For years, the field faced a trade-off between speed and reliability, because correcting errors inside a quantum computer slowed it down. That trade-off is fading fast, according to Rajeeb Hazra (pictured), chief executive officer of Quantinuum Inc., which listed on the Nasdaq in June.
“We are now at a stage in 2026 where we have the ability to have tremendous amounts of computation at a very high reliability rate,” Hazra said. “Just two weeks ago, we announced we were doing up to a million operations with five errors. To put it in contrast, just two years ago, we were trying to do 1,000 operations with one error. That’s how fast it is.”
Hazra spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Gemma Allen at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed advances in quantum error correction and how AI and quantum computing work in tandem. (* Disclosure below.)

Artificial Intelligence
Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
Many teams that build applications self-host their identity provider (IdP), such as Keycloak or PingFederate, inside a private network. These IdPs usually present a TLS server certificate from a private certificate authority (CA). With private CA support in AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, your agents can now connect to these IdPs while trusting the private CA that your organization already uses.
AgentCore Identity now supports private CA certificates for private identity providers. You store the PEM-encoded CA certificate in AWS Secrets Manager or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) and reference it from your credential provider. The CA certificate contains only the public certificate, not its private key. AgentCore Identity uses it to validate the server certificate presented by your IdP’s discovery, JSON Web Key Set (JWKS), and token endpoints. The CA certificate must be a root or intermediate CA certificate.
In this post, we show you how to issue an IdP certificate with AWS Private Certificate Authority. We then configure an AgentCore Identity credential provider to trust it and rotate the CA while minimizing downtime. “In the data center today, we have a lot of room for improvement of efficiency,” Virk said. “And when I say efficiency, I’m alluding to the wasted flops because we have GPU utilization that’s very low.”
Virk and Andy Mills (right), vice president of advanced product development at Penguin Solutions Inc., spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier and Amit Eyal Govrin at SC26, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. articles.title: AI finds Java flaw exposing banks, hospitals and companies
articles.summary:
AI has discovered an issue with Java that leaves many companies and other institutions vulnerable.
Using OpenAI’s still-not-public GPT-6 Cyber model, cybersecurity startup Calif found a string of “A” characters followed by an equals sign. While this normally leads to a crash, bad actors can leverage this to gain full unauthorized access to a device.
This is particular dangerous since Java is a ubiquitous programming language used by 90 per cent of Fortune 500 companies, including Amazon and Apple, as well as U.S. banks like J.P. Morgan Chase and the Bank of America and even hospitals.
Calif, for its part, says it’s not easy to use the bug for malicious purposes. Still, it’s an understandably big concern, and the agency says it’s been coordinating with associates in U.S., Canada, Australia, New Zealand and Britain accordingly. Oracle, which owns Java, hasn’t issues a public statement on the matter. Instead, it quietly rolled out a software patch on Tuesday.
This is the latest in a lineup of high-profile tech failures. Last week, Microsoft services like Outlook and Teams weren’t working for many people, which the company attributed to a “latent defect” from a server fix. The same week, U.S. airlines were grounded for hours due to air traffic control system errors.
Naturally, this has led experts to scrutinize the increasing role of AI in both tech businesses and those behind cyberattacks.

We then walk through a design pattern for the Explainability dimension, using a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) based customer support chatbot as the reference use case. This post implements one dimension, Explainability, in depth. Treat it as Part 1 of a series rather than a full build-out of all eight.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition makes it more straightforward to operationalize responsible AI through its native Aurora Machine Learning (Aurora ML) capabilities. With Aurora ML, you can invoke Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock foundation models directly from SQL, without data movement, custom extract, transform, and load (ETL) pipelines, or complex integrations. Zed is an open-source code editor written in Rust for macOS, Linux, and Windows by a team including the creators of GitHub’s Atom code editor, which was sunsetted in 2022, four years after Microsoft’s acquisition of GitHub. Zed touts a narrow focus on performance and user (i.e., developer) experience:

articles.title: TCL's 500Hz OLED panel fights burn-in while you're still using it
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Owning an OLED monitor these days requires a small chore. Every few hours, a pop-up asks you to let the screen shut off so it can recalibrate its pixels. That's how most of them keep burn-in at bay. TCL's display arm now has a 500Hz, 27-inch gaming panel that skips this task entirely by handling that upkeep in the background.
TCL CSOT showed off the prototype at its DTC2026 conference in Wuhan last week. It pairs the company's inkjet-printed OLED tech with an oxide backplane and what it calls the first in-panel compensation system built for high refresh rates. So rather than waiting for the monitor to go into standby, the panel keeps adjusting its pixels in real time.
Most OLED monitors today still handle that upkeep the old-fashioned way. Dell's Alienware AW3423DW, for instance, shows a reminder after four hours of use, asking you to run a refresh that turns the whole screen off. Skip those prompts long enough, and some models will simply force the cycle anyway.
Gaming screens were supposed to be the tricky case, though. After meeting the company at IFA in September, TFTCentral reported that this kind of internal compensation suited office monitors well. But sudden brightness swings in games meant those panels would probably still need a traditional pixel-cleaning cycle. The 500Hz prototype suggests TCL has found a way around that, at least on paper.

On one hand, engineers, financial analysts, legal teams, and operations staff are turning to generative and agentic AI to debug code, summarize contracts, and automate tasks and decision-making. Selon France Travail, seuls 6 % des dirigeants prévoient une automatisation importante où l’IA exécuterait la majorité des tâches humaines d’ici cinq ans. En revanche, 35 % des patrons considèrent cette technologie comme un assistant de travail, capable de libérer du temps sur la rédaction, la recherche ou l’analyse. Parmi les métiers les plus touchés, on compte ceux du numérique et des services intellectuels, avec 94 % des ingénieurs informatiques, 83 % des comptables et 75 % des bancassureurs concernés. À l’inverse, le BTP (80 % sans effet), les services aux particuliers (85 %) et la restauration (76 %) ne sont que très peu touchés.

It’s unclear if this app will be able to design an outfit based on stuff you’ve recently worn, the weather conditions or if it’ll offer details on what to wear based on your Calendar event. AA couldn’t enable the feature yet, and it’s unclear how far in development this feature is.
Still, I’ve always wanted something to do the work of putting outfits together for me. I’ve spent way too much brainpower on that.
Though, it’s worth noting that Google Photos ‘Wardrobe‘ functionality isn’t available in Canada yet, so it’ll probably take us Canadians even longer to get this feature.

Se trata de cuánto tiempo invertimos en nuestro trabajo y qué hacemos con el dinero obtenido. “Trabajamos para pagar cosas que no necesitamos”, dice Maxi Iglesias. Porque en este modo de gestionar nuestra vida siempre parece haber algo más que conseguir.
En la conversación, él mismo lo asocia a un problema de consumismo. Y para explicarlo utiliza la película “El club de la lucha” (David Fincher, 1999), protagonizada por Brad Pitt y Edward Norton.
Y en ella se asocia el hecho de ganar dinero con el de comprar cosas. De tal forma que si nuestras ambiciones materiales van en aumento, también tenemos que trabajar para ello. Es importante pararse a pensar en estas metas.
La obligación de sentirse productivo
Por otro lado, es relevante dejar claro que no hablamos de la vivienda. “Dejando el tema de la vivienda a un lado, somos muy autómatas en ese sentido, seguimos lo que el sistema nos ha dicho que hay que hacer: generar, producir, sentir que somos productivos, que hacemos y generamos”.
Hay que destacar esta idea de que tenemos que estar haciendo algo. Además de añadir metas a las anteriores. También es importante destacar que el problema está en que esperamos seguir creciendo sin saber dónde está el límite. “¿Hasta dónde se va a engordar la lista? ¿Hasta dónde se va a crecer?”, plantea.
Por otro lado, se puede reflexionar sobre el papel que tiene el trabajo en nuestra vida personal…

articles.title: Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its new security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft says is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).
STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”
The new Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.
This isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses …

articles.title: US closes the AI chip loophole that let China rent Nvidia hardware abroad
articles.summary:
Why it matters: US export controls on advanced AI chips have mostly focused on where the hardware ends up. Now, a new Commerce Department rule dictates who gets to use it. Under the rule, companies must get a license to ship chips from Nvidia and other US suppliers to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil, a move meant to stop Chinese customers from tapping data-center capacity in those countries over the network.
The gap the rule addresses is simple. A Chinese company that can't legally buy a cutting-edge Nvidia processor can still rent time on one, as long as the chip sits in a server rack outside China. The silicon never crosses the Chinese border, but the computing power does.
Firms such as Megaspeed International have built a business on that arrangement. They used billions of dollars' worth of Nvidia chips to build data centers across Southeast Asia, then sold the computing capacity to Chinese tech giants trying to catch up in artificial intelligence. Shutting down that channel is the main goal of the new rule.
"The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in a release.
The rule reaches beyond the five named countries, making it harder for data-center operators anywhere in the world to give Chinese companies remote access to AI chips. I…

De un terreno a un hogar. Después de unos cuantos años de búsqueda y de viajes, la pareja acabó convirtiendo un terreno de Los Hornillos, en el valle de Traslasierra, en su casa. Eso sí, aunque en algunas fases de la obra recibieron ayuda de otras personas, la mayor parte del trabajo la hicieron ellos solos.
Quincha y botellas bajo el suelo. Para las paredes utilizaron la quincha, una técnica de construcción que combina madera y paja para conseguir que la estructura tenga un buen aislamiento térmico.

articles.title: Windows will soon grade your PC's security, and apps like Battle.net get to see the score
articles.summary:
The big picture: Plenty of online PC games already refuse to launch unless Secure Boot is enabled. Microsoft now wants to turn checks like that into one standard question that any Windows 11 app can ask your PC. If the answer comes back no, the developer decides what happens next. Some apps may just show a warning; others could refuse to run altogether.
Microsoft calls the feature Windows baseline protection. Insiders can already try it, though a broader release isn't planned until 2027. None of the protections it checks are actually new. The feature simply rolls eight existing ones into a single pass-or-fail result. Those include TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, virtualization-based security, and memory integrity, along with a few rules that stop unsigned or known-flawed drivers from loading.
Ironically, Microsoft's own advice could trip up some gamers. Back in 2022, it suggested turning off memory integrity to claw back a few frames. Windows began switching the feature on automatically in October, but PCs where someone disabled it by hand are left alone, so those machines fail the check.
Secure Boot causes the same problem for anyone who switched it off to dual-boot Linux. Those PCs already can't play Battlefield 6, since its anti-cheat demands Secure Boot too.
Most of this can be fixed from a new Baseline protection page under Settings > Security. A single button there turns on whatever Windows can handle by itself, then restarts the PC. Secure Boot still means a trip into the UEFI m…

Why Groundcover’s CEO says agents are the power users of observability
An AI coding agent can write a patch in minutes. Ask it whether that patch slows down the API endpoint your customers hit most, and suddenly it needs something that lives outside the repository. It needs to see how the software runs.
That’s the premise behind Groundcover, an observability platform that wants to put production telemetry in the hands of developers and their coding agents. Yes, you read that correctly.
In a conversation with The New Stack’s Frederic Lardinois at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon this month in Salt Lake City, Groundcover CEO and co-founder Shahar Azulay explained why he thinks the same data engineers use to troubleshoot an incident can help an agent write and test a better change in the first place.

articles.title: Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing workload recovery and expanded infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
Large training jobs can fail even when every node looks healthy. A GPU with a subtle fault can pass its stress tests and still return wrong values. When a job stalls on an NCCL timeout, it keeps its GPUs, and Slurm still shows it as running. If a device plugin crashes on one node, the job fails with an error that never mentions the plugin. Teams usually find these problems only after the loss diverges or the job fails, and by then the compute is spent. Each of these failures lowers goodput, the share of your cluster’s time that goes to useful training. Today, we’re introducing workload recovery and infrastructure checks on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod that catch these failures sooner and raise the goodput of your training workloads.
SageMaker HyperPod already handles nodes that report hardware faults. The health monitoring agent (HMA) watches each node for GPU errors, deep health checks test nodes during provisioning, and automatic node recovery reboots or replaces faulty hardware. These features look at one node’s hardware at a time. They can’t tell whether the GPUs train correctly, whether a job is still making progress, or whether the Kubernetes components a job depends on are working.
In this post, we walk through the three new capabilities that catch these failures. For each one, we show how to set it up and what it reports when it finds a problem:

The Xbox Series S is the least powerful console; thus, the game runs at a lower base resolution of 720p, which is upscaled to 1080p using FSR 4. Artificial Intelligence
Full Fine-Tuning (FFT) on SageMaker AI Serverless Model Customization
Fine-tuning is the process of continuing to train a pretrained large language model (LLM) on a company’s own data so it adapts to a specific domain, task, or style rather than relying on general-purpose knowledge alone. For businesses, the value is twofold. A fine-tuned model delivers measurably better accuracy on domain-specific work while reducing costs: a smaller specialized model can match or exceed a frontier model on your task at a fraction of the per-token inference price. Those savings compound across millions of requests. Fine-tuning has therefore become an essential process for businesses looking to get more value from LLMs at lower costs.
Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods like Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) have emerged as a practical solution for fine-tuning LLMs to downstream tasks, reducing GPU capacity requirements by updating only a small subset of LLM parameters. LoRA aims to strike a balance between efficiency and expressiveness, however, the low-rank nature of the weight update inherently limits the representation power of LoRA fine-tuned models, potentially compromising performance on complex tasks. This trade-off hampers the ability of LoRA methods to capture complex patterns needed for diverse tasks. articles.title: Dos hombres desarrollaron psicosis y manía tras suspender un fármaco tipo Ozempic. La coincidencia inquieta a los médicos, aunque no demuestra nada
articles.summary:
Los fármacos GLP-1 tienen muchas luces, pero también muchas sombras. Llevan años ayudando a pacientes con diabetes a controlar sus niveles de glucosa y desde hace un tiempo también están ayudando a algunas personas a perder peso. Esto último ha llegado a rozar la obsesión en algunas personas, por lo que se advierte a quienes recurren a estos fármacos sin realmente necesitarlos que pueden tener un amplio abanico de efectos secundarios. La mayoría son leves, pero dos reportes de caso publicados recientemente en una revista de psiquiatría nos recuerdan que, en pacientes con problemas previos de salud mental, se debe reforzar la atención.
Ambos casos coinciden en que los pacientes dejaron de golpe un medicamento GLP-1 llamado tirzepatida y, poco después, desarrollaron síntomas psiquiátricos graves. Es cierto que tenían otros factores de riesgo y que, con solo dos casos, no podemos saber con seguridad si fue el medicamento el que causó el problema. Aun así, son una llamada de atención que nos recuerda la importancia de hacer un seguimiento aún más estricto en algunos pacientes receptores de los fármacos GLP-1.
Varón, 61 años. El primer caso es el de un hombre que dejó la tirzepatida, conocida comercialmente como Mounjaro, en agosto de 2025. Comenzó a sentir náuseas, así que abandonó el fármaco de golpe. articles.summary:
Nvidia GeForce driver bug reportedly hammers SSDs with up to 30GB of writes per hour — users trace massive idle wear to background service, newer driver reportedly still affected
That would use up to 5% of a typical 1TB SSD’s rated endurance each year.
Nvidia’s GeForce driver 621.14 is reportedly causing excessive background writes on idle PCs, inducing extra wear on SSDs. One user measured about 3GB an hour on the susceptible driver, and another mentioned estimated up to 30GB/hour on the newer 621.24. This follows a similar-looking bug from AMD’s video driver discovered last month.
The bug is described by user Andergraude in an Nvidia forum post as “new in 621.14,” which came out on Nov. 4, who says it operates by “continuously [rewriting] the binary log file” with “real writes” to the drive. The writes are coming from the NVDisplay.Container.exe process, or the “NVIDIA Display Container LS” service, which logs to the nvlog.nvlgstg file. This background service is necessary for running the Nvidia Control Panel and App. It’s not clear what’s written in the log, and not every system is necessarily impacted.
The “real writes” point comes from the fact that a per-process write counter is not the same as writes reaching the drive. The measurements came from Windows Resource Monitor, Windows performance counters, and CrystalDiskInfo. The Data Units Written counter matched Windows’ reporting. articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a distance of one light-day from Earth
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first human-made object to travel one light-day from Earth. The milestone occurred on November 18 at 5:16:07 a.m. Eastern time, roughly nine years before its twin spacecraft, Voyager 2, will achieve the same feat.
One "day" might not sound like a lot of time or distance, and in the vast emptiness of space, where everything is so far apart, it really isn't. Rather than using familiar measurements such as miles or kilometers, distances in space are often described in terms of how light travels.
Light moves through space at approximately 186,000 miles per second, and nothing travels faster. The Moon, for reference, is roughly 238,855 miles from Earth on average, and it takes light about 1.3 seconds to travel that distance. At 93 million miles away, sunlight takes about eight minutes and 20 seconds to reach our planet. Astronomers also use the latter, called an astronomical unit (or AU for short), as a unit of length in space.
As you might have guessed, a light-day is the distance light travels in 24 hours: 16,094,799,096 miles (25,902,068,356 kilometers), to be exact. A light-year, by comparison, is roughly 5.88 trillion miles.
NASA launched the two Voyager probes in 1977 to study planets in the outskirts of our solar system, including gas giants Jupiter and Saturn. articles.title: HPC meets AI agents as Google Cloud targets time to discovery - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google Cloud brings AI agents to the supercomputing bottleneck
High-performance computing, or HPC, is merging with artificial intelligence faster than many research teams can adapt. Compute capacity is hard to get, and workloads now run across clouds and on-premises clusters. The metric that matters is shifting from peak performance to time to discovery.
That shift is on full display as supercomputing and AI converge at SC26 in Chicago. articles.summary:
C'est une escroquerie de grande ampleur qui vient d'être démantelée par le FBI. Elle utilisait des vidéos de gens connus de la victime pour la pousser à télécharger un programme malveillant.
On n'arrête jamais le progrès dans le monde des escroqueries internet. On avait ainsi découvert le mois dernier l'escroquerie au faux support Microsoft, qui opérait depuis quasiment une décennie, et avait permis aux malfaiteurs de générer plusieurs millions de dollars. Mais il y a pourtant beaucoup plus impressionnant encore, comme on peut le voir avec cette annonce du FBI.
Une escroquerie par Zoom volant le visage des proches des victimes démantelée par le FBI
La FBI vient d'annoncer le démantelement d'une vaste infrastructure d'escroquerie, dans le cadre de l'opération « FaceStealer ». Une escroquerie au fonctionnement particulièrement sophistiquée.
Celle-ci commence par le vol de l'identité d'une personne connue de la victime, ou d'un professionnel connu dans son secteur. Cette fausse personnalité sollicite la victime via un message sur LinkedIn ou Telegram, puis l'invite à une conférence Zoom ou Teams. La victime intègre alors une conférence dans laquelle elle voit en vidéo la personne qui est connue, une vidéo prise précédemment par les pirates, avec d'autres participants aussi présents.
À un moment, l'un d'eux explique ne pas entendre le micro de la victime, ce qui est suivi par l'apparition d'un message d'erreur l'invitant à télécharger une mise à jour… qui est en fait un malware.

"What's going on?!" my commuter friend asked me, wild-eyed. "They told us to start stockpiling water, go to the bank, take out our money!" When I asked her who, she mentioned a mainstream media outlet.
I locked eyes with her to make sure I had her full attention: "Don't do that. This is not a calamity. It's not the end of the tech world."
"But… but… it's all happening. How could it all happen at once?"

Security experts Symantec have outlined how they saw attackers targeting victims with typosquatted names of popular companies such as CarMax, McDonald’s, and Procter & Gamble.
Many people don’t pay close attention to spelling or typos, and threat actors turned it into a criminal enterprise. A malicious executable called Excsel.exe has a higher chance of being launched compared to one called malware-v2.exe. App do Gemini agora funciona até em celulares Android com pouca RAM
Google otimizou aplicativo do Gemini para funcionar em celulares Android básicos com pelo menos 2 GB de RAM.
O aplicativo oficial do Gemini para Android foi lançado no começo de 2024, logo após o serviço deixar de se chamar Bard (lembra disso?). Mas usuários de celulares Android mais simples ficavam restritos ao Google Assistente Go, com comandos básicos. Bom, não mais: o Google tratou de otimizar a ferramenta para que ela funcione até com aparelhos Android básicos, com 2 GB de RAM ou mais.
É importante deixar claro desde já que não estamos falando de um aplicativo alternativo do Gemini voltado especificamente a dispositivos de entrada. O que o Google fez foi tornar o aplicativo oficial do serviço capaz de funcionar a contento mesmo quando houver capacidade reduzida de memória RAM ou armazenamento.
O Google explica que, até recentemente, as limitações de hardware impediam que esses dispositivos rodassem o app do Gemini, deixando o usuário acessar, no máximo, comandos básicos de voz no antigo assistente.

Ce 17 novembre, la start-up californienne Calif a dévoilé une brèche dans le cœur du code de Java, un langage de programmation omniprésent dans le monde entier. Baptisée Java4Shell, la faille permet à un pirate de prendre le contrôle de certains serveurs à distance. Elle touche surtout les serveurs des entreprises équipés de processeurs Intel ou AMD récents. Les puces ARM, présentes dans la plupart des smartphones, ne sont pas concernées.

Conscient de la difficulté de la tâche, il s’est tourné vers Codex, l’assistant d’OpenAI propulsé par GPT-6 Cyber, un modèle d’IA spécialisé dans la recherche de failles.
 Since the vulnerability has leaked: Calif discovered and reported Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938).

Dos fallas de seguridad en CreditNirvana, una plataforma india que usa inteligencia artificial para cobrar deudas, dejaron expuestas 6,6 millones de cuentas de deudores y unas 315.000 grabaciones de llamadas. El investigador independiente Eaton Zveare las descubrió, y WIRED las dio a conocer el 18 de noviembre.
CreditNirvana pertenece a Perfios, una empresa india de tecnología financiera. Su sistema decide cuál es el siguiente paso con cada deudor y lo ejecuta sin intervención humana, según la propia descripción citada por WIRED.
Zveare informó los problemas a CERT-In, el equipo de respuesta a emergencias informáticas de India, el 30 de mayo. Según su cronología, las fallas se corrigieron el 2 de junio, un día después de que la empresa las conoció. CERT-In emitió la nota oficial con los identificadores de las vulnerabilidades el 26 de octubre.
CERT-In clasificó una falla como de gravedad alta y la otra como crítica. WIRED informó que CreditNirvana y Perfios no respondieron a sus pedidos de comentarios.
Un código mal protegido abría el centro de llamadas
La primera falla afectaba al centro de llamadas con agentes de IA que usa la financiera Aditya Birla Capital Finance. El sitio pedía iniciar sesión, pero una clave de acceso estaba escrita en el código de la página y daba control total, según el informe de Zveare.

articles.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
articles.summary:
A malicious widget can bypass the security filter that Telegram added to its Android app last week and run code outside it, according to NebuSec, a security company.
Widgets are small interactive blocks that bots send inside chat messages, and their JavaScript runs on the user's phone. The researchers ran their demonstration on a Telegram test server, because only approved bots can send widgets on the live service now.
Bots could start sending widgets last week. Two days later, an account called V12 posted a video on X claiming that any Telegram message could now be used to execute remote code.
Telegram then put QuickJS, the small engine that runs widget JavaScript, into its own process on Android. It also added a seccomp filter, which can block or record the system calls that the process makes. Both changes appear in the source code it published for Telegram for Android 13.2.2 (7303).
NebuSec said in a technical analysis published earlier this week that its researchers got code running outside that filter in two separate ways. One uses a widget bug the filter does not cover, and the other chains a widget bug the filter does cover with a kernel bug.
In their video, a bot's Telegram widget on Android 13.2.2 (7303) bypasses the filter and opens the phone's calculator app, the researchers say.
Their write-up and their demonstration post on X do not say what the code could reach beyond that, such as the app's messages or the rest of the phone. They also do not say whether the use…

La copia de seguridad en el teléfono puede hacerse de varias formas en Android: a través de la nube de Google, mediante aplicaciones de sincronización local o con una transferencia manual por cable USB hacia una computadora.
Cada método tiene ventajas distintas según el tipo de archivo que se quiera proteger y la facilidad que se busque en el proceso.
Qué ofrece la copia de seguridad con la cuenta de Google
Android incorpora, desde la versión 9, una función nativa de respaldo que no requiere aplicaciones adicionales. Se accede desde Ajustes, luego Google y la opción Copia de Seguridad y Restauración.
Allí es posible elegir entre una copia manual inmediata, con el botón “Hacer copia de seguridad ahora”, o una programación automática dividida en dos bloques: Fotos y Vídeos, gestionado por Google Fotos, y Otros Datos del Dispositivo, que incluye mensajes SMS y MMS, historial de llamadas, ajustes del sistema y aplicaciones con sus datos. Los contactos se sincronizan de forma separada con la cuenta de Google.
El almacenamiento gratuito que ofrece Google para estas copias es de 15 gigabytes, un límite compartido con Gmail y Drive. Quien necesite más espacio puede contratar un plan de Google One, cuyo escalón mínimo ofrece 100 GB.

articles.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
articles.summary:
Threat actors have compromised Microsoft's agent-framework package to push a credential stealer, according to reports from Aikido, Chainguard, Endor Labs, OX Security, SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Google-owned Wiz.
The malicious versions, 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, were published 33 minutes apart on November 17, 2026, and are designed to run a credential stealer on every Python start. As of writing, both the release versions have been quarantined on the Python Package Index (PyPI) repository. It's unclear how the attacker managed to obtain publishing access.
Agent-framework is the meta-package for Microsoft Agent Framework, an open-source framework for building and orchestrating artificial intelligence (AI) agents using Python.
"Both versions install Python startup hooks that silently collect credentials, environment data, and cloud identity tokens, then exfiltrate them to a webhook[.]site endpoint," Socket said in a report.
Once either of the versions is installed, the package drops a .pth file in the site-packages root directory, which then gets executed automatically on every interpreter start, causing the credential stealer to run whenever Python is started in an environment, even if the package is not explicitly imported.
"Each wheel adds a .pth file to site-packages," Endor Labs said. "Python executes import lines in .pth files on every interpreter start, so the stealer runs on any Python launch in an affected environment, including pip itself, whether or not anything imp…

articles.title: CISA Urges Immediate Patching of Java4Shell Flaw That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
articles.summary:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has urged organizations to immediately patch a newly disclosed critical security flaw impacting Oracle Java.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-114938 (CVSS score: 8.1), refers to a case of out-of-bounds write that can lead to denial-of-service (DoS) or remote code execution under certain conditions.
"This critical memory-corruption vulnerability, known as 'Java4Shell,' affects the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which is part of the Java Development Kit (JDK)," CISA said. "Specially crafted Base64 input could crash the JVM and allow for unauthenticated remote code execution."
Patches for the flaw have been released by Oracle and OpenJDK. As of writing, there is no evidence the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild.
As reported previously by The Hacker News, Java4Shell can enable attackers without an account to execute arbitrary code on Keycloak, Atlassian Jira, Atlassian Confluence, JFrog Artifactory, Jenkins, and PingFederate, and with a login on Apache Kafka Broker, Apache Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker, under default settings.
Advisories for the flaw have been released by numerous security and software vendors, including Aikido, Amazon Linux, Blackpoint Cyber, Chainguard, Cisco Talos, Cycode, Datadog, Dynatrace, Endor Labs, Field Effect, Hadrian, Horizon3.ai, Miggo, Orca Security, Qualys, Rapid7, Red Hat, SentinelOne, Sophos, Tanium, Tenable, Upwind, VulnCheck, …

A Java flaw called Java4Shell can let attackers without an account run their own code on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, and three other widely used applications, says Calif, the security research firm that disclosed it this week.
The flaw is present in Java 17.0.6 and later, and the vulnerable code runs only on x86-64 Intel and AMD chips that support the AVX-512 VBMI feature.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114938, the fix was released today by Oracle and the OpenJDK project, whose open-source code underpins Java builds from many vendors. Amazon has fixed its Corretto Java builds, but Red Hat is still preparing fixes for its own.
The researchers are holding back their attack code for the six applications, and other labs have so far reproduced crashes and a memory leak but not the code execution. Canada's Cyber Center said this week that it was not aware of any attacks exploiting the flaw.
Servers often decode Base64-encoded data, such as HTTP Basic login headers, SAML artifacts, and CSRF tokens, before checking whether a user is logged in. That is how an attacker without an account can exploit the flaw.
The flaw is in a faster version of Java's Base64 decoder that runs on chips with AVX-512 VBMI. Java switches to it after compiling the decoder for speed, which it does for code that runs often.
A malformed string that ends with an extra = makes this decoder write 62 or 63 bytes past the end of its output. Java rejects the string, but only after the write.

articles.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
articles.summary:
On AMD-based PCs and some Intel PCs, the TPM lockout for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs can be reset by someone who opens the PC's case, researchers at Technische Universität Berlin say.
That leaves short PINs open to guessing. In lab tests, the researchers found a four-digit Hello PIN on an AMD laptop and a 6-digit BitLocker PIN on an Intel laptop this way.
Both PINs were set by the researchers and found within 236 tries. From the speeds they measured, they calculate a worst-case of 40 hours for a four-digit Hello PIN, compared to 69 days with the lockout working as documented. For a default six-digit BitLocker PIN, the worst-case time drops from 19 years to 20 days.
AMD confirmed yesterday that its processor firmware has a flaw that allows the attack on some PCs with its chips. It plans fixes for most of those chips between November and February 2027. For now, the researchers advise adding at least two digits to Hello and BitLocker PINs.
The TPM in these PCs is a firmware TPM, built into the processor. Unlike a separate TPM chip, it has no secure storage of its own, according to the research paper the researchers posted late last week. So it keeps its saved state, including the count of wrong guesses, encrypted on the mainboard's flash chip.
If someone copies that saved state and later writes the old copy back, the count goes back too, unless the PC detects it. Newer PCs try to catch this with counters inside the flash chip, called RPMC, that can only go up.

articles.title: Today I learned a single Google Gemini query uses about five drops of water, but that's not the whole truth
articles.summary:
Today I learned a single Google Gemini query uses about five drops of water, but that's not the whole truth
Google's per-prompt figure skips the water power plants use
Asking Gemini to rewrite your email costs about five drops of water. At least, that's what Google says.
In an August 2025 technical paper, the company estimated that a median Gemini Apps text prompt uses 0.24 Wh of energy, emits 0.03 grams of CO2 equivalent and consumes 0.26 mL of water.
Google compared the energy use to watching TV for less than nine seconds. It also claimed that over a 12-month period, the energy and carbon footprint of a median prompt fell by 33x and 44x respectively. Those are big efficiency gains, assuming the math holds up.
A technically correct figure
Credit where it's due, Google's method counts more than most. Alongside the AI chips themselves, it includes host CPUs and memory, idle machines kept on standby, plus data center overhead like cooling. If you count only active TPUs and GPUs, the numbers drop to 0.10 Wh and 0.12 mL, which Google itself calls an underestimate.
By Google's own breakdown, the AI accelerators account for 58% of the energy behind each prompt. Host CPUs and memory take another 24%, with spare capacity and data center overhead making up the remaining 18%.
The catch is in the water. Google's figure covers only the water consumed on-site to cool its data centers, calculated from its 2024 fleetwide average. The fine print also notes that the data hasn't been verified …

articles.title: Critical Apache Roller RCE Flaw Under Active Exploitation, No Authentication Required
articles.summary:
A critical security flaw in Apache Roller, an open-source, Java-based blogging platform, has come under active exploitation in the wild, according to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF)
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS score: 9.8), is a case of unauthenticated deserialization in the XML-RPC endpoint that could lead to remote code execution.
"Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code," project maintainers said. "The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester."
ASF also noted that the vulnerability is the same as CVE-2026-82384 (CVSS score: 9.8), which was patched in September 2026 and listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected.
"This issue is being actively exploited," it added. ASF did not share any details on how the vulnerability is being exploited, or who is being targeted as part of these efforts.
A security researcher named n0mi1k has been credited with finding the flaw, and Matt Raible has been acknowledged for reporting it.
Users are advised to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.
If immediate patching is not an option, it's recommended to set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and then restart Roller.

articles.title: F5 Warns 6 Critical BIG-IP Flaws Can Crash Traffic in Specific Setups, May Allow RCE
articles.summary:
Six critical vulnerabilities in F5 BIG-IP allow an attacker to crash the Traffic Management Microkernel (TMM) without logging in, disrupting traffic until the TMM restarts.
Each flaw needs a specific setup on a virtual server: an iRule that uses a particular command, or an APM policy that includes two particular kinds of agent.
F5, which makes BIG-IP, disclosed the flaws today and says they may also allow remote code execution. The company has released engineering hotfixes and lists no workaround.
The company rates all six 9.8 under CVSS v3.1 and 9.3 under CVSS v4.0. They are stack-based buffer overflows in BIG-IP's data plane, the part that processes almost all of its network traffic. The management side is not exposed, according to the company.
None of the company's advisories says the flaws have been exploited. WatchTowr researcher Sina Kheirkhah reported four, and the company found the other two itself.
Five of the flaws are in iRules, a BIG-IP feature that administrators use to manage traffic, and one is in BIG-IP's APM module. Some also affect BIG-IP Next for Kubernetes and BIG-IP CNF, part of the company's BIG-IP Cloud-Native Edition.
Each flaw needs the setup listed below on a virtual server:
- CVE-2026-123637: an APM per-request policy that includes both the Client Information agent and Endpoint Security agents. Affects BIG-IP APM only.

Sur le forum officiel de NVIDIA, un utilisateur a mesuré environ 515 Mo d’écritures en cinq minutes d’inactivité avec cette version, contre moins de 2 Mo avec la 621.01. articles.title: PHP Warns of Critical Security Flaws Affecting All Supported Versions, Fixes Coming November 19
articles.summary:
The maintainers of the PHP programming language on Wednesday issued an advisory announcing an upcoming security release that addresses critical flaws.
The release is scheduled for November 19, 2026, between 2 and 2:30 p.m. UTC.
"These releases are part of PHP's regular four-week release cycle and will address security vulnerabilities affecting all supported PHP versions," the maintainers said. "The highest severity is CRITICAL."
However, the project also noted that issues rated critical require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups. It did not disclose any additional specifics.
However, it's expected to include CVE-2026-115560, a remote code execution flaw that succeeds only if the following conditions are met -
- An application sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration, and its code switches the handler to php with ini_set() before calling session_start().
- Session upload progress is enabled, which is PHP's default.
As mitigations, users were urged to set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and restart the PHP worker for the setting to be applied.
The development comes nearly a month after PHP released fixes for two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, collectively tracked as PHP2Shell that enable unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via specially crafted HTTP requests.

articles.title: Java4Shell CVE-2026-114938 qué saber y cómo corregir este fallo en seguridad
articles.summary:
Una vulnerabilidad crítica identificada como CVE-2026-114938 y bautizada Java4Shell afecta al decodificador Base64 de la máquina virtual HotSpot para x86-64, la implementación de referencia que forma parte del kit de desarrollo de Java.
La Agencia de Ciberseguridad e Infraestructura de Estados Unidos (CISA) pide tratarla como urgencia operativa, ya que una entrada Base64 manipulada puede tumbar la máquina virtual y, en determinadas condiciones, permitir que un atacante remoto ejecute código sin autenticarse en el proceso que la aloja.
El problema de fondo no es solo técnico, sino de visibilidad: Java no aparece en los inventarios como una aplicación, sino como una dependencia dentro de otras aplicaciones, lo que complica saber dónde está instalado y, por tanto, dónde corregirlo.
Qué es Java4Shell y por qué afecta al decodificador Base64
Java4Shell no es un fallo en una aplicación concreta, sino en una pieza que atraviesa casi todo el software moderno. Base64 es el componente que convierte datos binarios en texto para que viajen por correo, por una cabecera HTTP o dentro de un documento XML.
Esa omnipresencia es justo lo que agrava el fallo. Al estar en el camino de entrada de casi todo, un error en su decodificador no necesita que la aplicación exponga nada especial: basta con que acepte datos procedentes del exterior.

El despliegue técnico importa porque el nuevo título llegará a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S con una ambición que abarca desde la iluminación hasta el comportamiento del agua, la vegetación y el tráfico. Rockstar busca que cada recorrido, persecución o pausa frente al paisaje responda a condiciones cambiantes del entorno.
El trazado de rayos cambia la luz en Leonida y Vice City
El avance más visible está en la iluminación global. GTA 6 incorpora trazado de rayos en tiempo real para calcular el comportamiento de la luz sobre distintas superficies, según la hora del día y el estado del clima.
Los reflejos sobre el asfalto tras una tormenta tropical, las luces de neón sobre los vehículos y el brillo del océano en Vice City dependerán de condiciones dinámicas. Este sistema evita que esos efectos se limiten a recursos visuales precalculados.
La evolución del motor RAGE, sigla de Rockstar Advanced Game Engine, también se aprecia en el detalle de los materiales. La piel, el sudor, la ropa y las superficies desgastadas presentan una representación más cercana a la de producciones cinematográficas.

articles.title: Microsoft ofreció a 60.000 empleados irse de la empresa y Nadella dijo que no puede prometer que todo seguirá igual
articles.summary:
El director ejecutivo de Microsoft, Satya Nadella, explicó por qué la compañía ofreció una salida voluntaria a unos 60.000 empleados. “Desearía poder sentarme aquí y decir que todo será igual. No puedo”, afirmó esta semana en el pódcast The Pragmatic Engineer, al referirse al impacto de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en el trabajo.
La oferta se anunció el 26 de octubre mediante un mensaje de la directora de personal, Amy Coleman. Está dirigida a trabajadores de Canadá, India, Reino Unido y Estados Unidos hasta el nivel interno 70, que incluye a algunos gerentes generales y vicepresidentes, según el comunicado de la empresa.
Microsoft confirmó a GeekWire que los 60.000 empleados elegibles representan cerca de una cuarta parte de su plantilla, que al 30 de junio ascendía a 223.000 personas, de acuerdo con los informes anuales citados por el medio. Solo participan algunas áreas y cada organización decide si adhiere al programa.
El paquete equivale a la indemnización habitual de la compañía e incluye salario base según la antigüedad y el nivel, continuidad en la entrega de acciones, cobertura de salud por un período fijo y asesoría para la búsqueda de empleo. Los trabajadores tienen hasta la primera semana de diciembre para responder a la propuesta.
Microsoft calcula que menos del 5 % aceptará la salida voluntaria

articles.title: OpenAI aurait perdu le contrôle de ses agents IA... plus de 80 fois
articles.summary:
La Californie poursuit OpenAI en justice. Elle lui reproche d’avoir testé des modèles d’IA sans protections ni surveillance suffisantes. Cela aurait permis à des agents autonomes de sortir de leur environnement d’essai et de s’introduire chez des tiers.
Le procureur général Rob Bonta a déposé plainte le 16 novembre contre OpenAI Foundation et OpenAI Group PBC. Il part de l’attaque contre Hugging Face en juillet et affirme qu’OpenAI lui a elle-même reconnu plus de 80 pertes de contrôle pendant ses tests.
Un forum improvisé, 17 600 actions et des alertes restées sans suite
OpenAI entraînait ses agents IA dans des « bacs à sable », des environnements censés les isoler d’internet. Comme d’autres développeurs, l’entreprise teste souvent ses modèles avec moins de garde-fous que les versions diffusées au public, afin d’en mesurer toutes les capacités. Sont retirés, par exemple, les systèmes qui poussent l’agent à rester dans son périmètre ou qui font examiner les actions exigeant des autorisations spéciales. Selon la plainte, ce retrait imposait un cloisonnement plus strict, et OpenAI a admis que ces protections auraient pu limiter l’attaque. Or, plusieurs agents partageaient un même service de paquets logiciels, mal configuré. Ils l’ont détourné en forum improvisé, où ils s’échangeaient des informations, et une faille leur a aussi ouvert l’accès à internet. Environ 1 200 agents ont fréquenté ce forum et près de 700 ont attaqué Hugging Face en juillet : 17 600 actions en deux jours …

articles.title: “Le deseo lo mejor a Jensen y a Nvidia. El mundo no necesita opiniones aleatorias sobre lo que va a suceder”, Sam Altman
articles.summary:
Directivos del sector tecnológico expresaron su solidaridad con Jensen Huang durante la cumbre DealBook, luego de que este dimitiera de Nvidia la semana pasada tras conocerse su relación extramatrimonial con una mujer que, según la inteligencia estadounidense, sería una agente china.
Ahora bien, el propio Huang no asistió al evento, pero su ausencia marcó buena parte de las intervenciones.
Entre quienes salieron en su defensa estuvieron Sam Altman, de OpenAI, y Palmer Luckey, de Anduril, según recogió The New York Times. Ambos coincidieron en respaldar al ejecutivo, aunque con matices distintos sobre las razones de su apoyo y las consecuencias que podría tener su salida para la industria de la inteligencia artificial.
Qué dijeron Sam Altman y Palmer Luckey sobre la salida de Jensen Huang
Sam Altman evitó sumarse a las especulaciones sobre el futuro de Nvidia tras la salida de su fundador. En diálogo con Andrew Ross Sorkin, señaló: “Le deseo lo mejor a Jensen. Le deseo lo mejor a Nvidia. No creo que el mundo necesite otro conjunto de opiniones aleatorias sobre lo que va a suceder aquí”.
El director ejecutivo de OpenAI relacionó la situación con su propia experiencia como destituido y luego restituido en su cargo, en 2023. Según explicó, ese episodio le permitió comprender mejor lo que atraviesa Huang: “Algo que no me gustó fue que todo el mundo estuviera especulando con alguna teoría al azar aquí y allá”.

articles.title: Cuántos dólares vale el Cybercab de Tesla sin pedales y qué servicios se pagan mensuales
articles.summary:
Tesla comenzó a aceptar pedidos del público para el Cybercab, su vehículo totalmente autónomo para uso personal, a un precio base de USD 29.990. A esa cifra se suma una suscripción obligatoria de USD 299 mensuales por el sistema de conducción autónoma, sin la cual, según los términos y condiciones de la empresa, “su Cybercab no funcionará”.
El anuncio, realizado la semana pasada, adelantó que las entregas comenzarán el próximo mes. La decisión sorprendió porque sugiere que la compañía acelera los planes de su director ejecutivo, Elon Musk, de consolidar un futuro basado en vehículos autónomos e inteligencia artificial.
Cuánto cuesta el Cybercab de Tesla y por qué incluye una cuota mensual
El Cybercab tiene un costo de compra de USD 29.990, pero ese monto no cubre el funcionamiento completo del vehículo. Para que el sistema de conducción autónoma esté operativo, los propietarios deben pagar además una suscripción mensual de USD 299.
Sin ese pago adicional, el auto queda inhabilitado. Así lo establecen los términos y condiciones de Tesla, que condicionan el uso del vehículo a mantener activa la suscripción.
El propio Musk cuestionó ese valor. En una publicación en redes sociales difundida este fin de semana, sostuvo que el costo mensual es “demasiado elevado” y que debería acercarse al precio de la suscripción de conducción automatizada con conectividad premium que Tesla ofrece en otros modelos, cercano a los USD 115 mensuales.
